info.title: Yalla API
info.description:
Table reservation and in-app ordering for restaurants and cafes. Consumed by the diner app, the staff tablet and the admin panel.

Conventions: money is a whole count of Armenian dram (properties suffixed `Amd`); every instant is UTC; wall-clock values (opening hours, the local date and time on a booking) are dates and times in the branch's own time zone and are never converted; enums are integers matching the database, with each member documented on the schema.

Every failure is an RFC 7807 problem document. Branch on its `code`, which is a stable slug, never on the message.

get.summary: The console's Messages page: the branch's threads with guests over the last year
get.description:
Read only - nobody answers from here (replies go from the tablet), and **nothing is marked read**: the tablet's unread counts stay as they were. The right pane is the thread's own staff read, `getStaffReservationConversation` / `getStaffTakeawayConversation`, which never marks read either.

Query, all optional: `from`, `to` - branch-local dates, `yyyy-MM-dd`, inclusive, matched against the day of the thread's **last** message on the branch's clock; `to` defaults to today and `from` to six days before `to`. `from` is not after `to`, the range is at most 366 days, and neither is before today - 365 (older threads are deleted, see `docs/messages.md` §history). `kind`: `all` (default), `reservation` or `takeaway`. `q`: at most 60 characters, case-insensitive - the guest's name (contains), the table (exact) or the takeaway code (`T-482` or `482`). `unansweredOnly`: `true` keeps the threads whose guest's last typed message has no venue message (text or ask) after it. `limit`: 1 to 100, default 50. `cursor`: the page before's `nextCursor`. A bad value is **422 `validation-failed`** naming every bad field in `context.fields` (`from`, `to`, `kind`, `q`, `unansweredOnly`, `cursor`, `limit`).

Answers `{ items, nextCursor, from, to }` - `from` and `to` the dates read, defaults filled in; `nextCursor` absent on the last page. Newest last message first, then by thread, so equal instants neither repeat nor skip across pages; a thread written to after the first page moves above the cursor and shows on a fresh read. Each item: `conversationId`, `subject` (`kind`, `id`, `label` - the table or the `T-` code, `guestName`, `localDate`, `localTime` - a booking's start or an order's ready time, `partySize` or `itemCount`/`totalAmd`, and `outcome`: a booking `came`, `no-show`, `cancelled`, `declined` or `upcoming`; an order `collected`, `no-show`, `declined`, `cancelled` or `in-progress`), `messageCount` (the guest's and the venue's - not the system's status lines), `firstAtUtc`, `lastAtUtc`, `lastLocal` (`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` on the branch's clock), `staffNames` (who at the venue wrote, as they were named then, each once in the order they first wrote), `unanswered`, `open`.

Manager or above, scoped like the Reviews page: a branch manager reaches their own branch only, the owner and the general manager every branch of their venue, a platform admin any. Waiters and the kitchen: 403.

post.summary: Upload a photo for a menu item or a venue card
post.description:
Multipart upload of a single `file` part. Returns the photo id and its three variant URLs; attach the id to a menu item or a branch.

**The bytes are sniffed, never trusted.** JPEG, PNG and WebP are accepted and everything else is refused, whatever the declared content type or the file name says - those are both attacker-controlled.

**EXIF is stripped.** A menu photo comes off the owner's phone carrying GPS coordinates and a device serial; the original bytes are never stored. Three variants are generated and the originals are discarded.

Uploading the same image twice returns the first photo and writes nothing, with `wasDeduplicated: true`. A photo nothing attaches to is deleted after 24 hours.

get.summary: Pending, failed and dead-lettered message counts
get.description:
**The first place to look when notifications quietly stop working.** Without it the symptom is silence, and silence is indistinguishable from nothing having happened.

`deadLettered` is the number that needs a person: those have been given up on and will never be retried. Each carries its last error and the key that names what caused it, so a dead reminder can be traced back to its booking.

A `sentLastDay` of zero on a live venue means the channel is broken, whatever the other counts say.

post.summary: Generate a one-time code for enrolling a tablet
post.description:
The code is returned **once**. Only its hash is stored, so a manager who loses it issues another rather than looking it up.

It is good for 24 hours and exactly one redemption. Codes get read out across a bar and will be overheard; single use is what makes that survivable, because a second redemption fails and the manager sees a tablet in the list they did not enrol.

get.summary: Every tablet and personal phone enrolled to this branch
get.description:
Revoked devices are included, so the list is an audit trail rather than a roster.

`kind` narrows it: `1` tablets, `2` personal phones; absent, both. Each item says its `kind`; a phone also names its person in `boundStaffMember` (`id`, `fullName`, `role`), and its `name` is what the phone called itself when it paired - its platform and browser in English, "iPhone · Safari" - and `platform` and `browser` are the same as parts, for the console to word in its reader's language (absent on a phone paired before them; read `name` then). `lastSeenAtUtc` moves with every PIN sign-in and session renewal on the device; `revokedAtUtc` is when it was revoked or unpaired.

post.summary: Show a QR that pairs one person's own phone to them
post.description:
Returns `{ code, expiresAtUtc, pairingUrl, staffMemberId, branchId }` **once**: only the code's hash is stored. `code` is ten characters shown as `XXXXX-XXXXX`; `pairingUrl` is what the QR carries - the staff app's `/staff/pair#code=XXXXX-XXXXX` on the console's own origin, the code in the fragment so it never reaches a server log. The phone redeems it with the person's own PIN (`POST /api/auth/staff/phone-pair`).

**Ten minutes and one use.** Issuing another code for the same person supersedes their unused one, so *show a new code* takes a lost one back.

**Who may.** Manager or above, from their stored row, by the staff-admin rules: the person must be someone the caller may manage, or the caller themselves - a general manager pairs branch managers, waiters and themselves, never an owner. A branch manager pairs at their own branch, and only their own branch's people. The person must sign in at this branch (at it, or venue-wide) - anybody else is 404 here - and be active.

**Not kitchen staff**: `409 kitchen-phone-not-allowed`. The kitchen stays on its tablet.

Audited as `staff.phone-pairing-issued` (who, for whom, which branch, the expiry - never the code). Rate limited like the other credential routes (`auth`).

post.summary: Kill a lost or stolen tablet, or unpair somebody's phone
post.description:
Takes effect on the tablet's next request, not when its token expires - every request carrying a device or session token checks this row. Any session open on the tablet is ended at the same time, because the session is the thing that can act.

Permanent. A tablet that turns up again is enrolled afresh.

The same for a personal phone (`kind` 2): unpairing it ends its session now, and it is paired again only with a new code. A phone's unpairing is audited as `staff.phone-unpaired`.

get.summary: A branch's bookings in one status - the approval queue
get.description:
What the console's *awaiting approval* panel reads before calling `approve` or `reject`. `status` is required (`1` PendingApproval).

Sorted by the branch's local date, then local start time. **No paging: at most 200 rows**, the earliest first, so what a cap would cut is what is furthest away.

Manager or above: a branch manager lists their own branch only; an owner or general manager, any branch of their venue; a platform admin, any branch. (Approving and rejecting are open to the branch's waiters too; the floor's own list is `/reservations/awaiting`.) `awaitingApprovalBecause` is the reason stored when the booking went to approval - worked out against the branch's current policy only for a booking from before that was stored - and `approvalExpiresAtUtc` the deadline to count down to: fifteen minutes at short notice, two hours for a booking waiting on the guest before it (`awaitingApprovalBecause` 5). `awaitsEarlierGuestAnswer` true means that guest answers in the app and only they can - approve and reject are `409 reservation-awaiting-earlier-guest` - so show the countdown, not the buttons; false, the floor decides it after calling them.

post.summary: Change the signed-in venue user's password
post.description:
The platform admin's change, for the venue console. `currentPassword` must be right and `newPassword` at least 12 characters - the one rule every console password follows. Everything wrong is reported in one 422: a wrong current password is `context.fields` naming `currentPassword` with `bound` `conflict`, not a 401, so the console stays signed in and shows it under the field.

**Answers a fresh token pair - store it.** The change ends every session the account has, at once: the session generation moves, so every admin-panel access token it holds - the one this request was sent with included - is refused from now on with `401 session-revoked`, every refresh token is revoked and every unused reset link is spent. The body (`accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresInSeconds`, the refresh endpoint's shape) is how the sign-in that made the change carries on.

**Wrong current passwords are counted per account**: each is audited as `account.password-change-failed`, and after 10 inside 15 minutes the route answers `429 too-many-attempts` with `Retry-After` (and `context.retryAfterSeconds`) until the oldest leaves the window - right password or not. A successful change starts the count again. The route is also under the `auth` rate limit. **Audited** as `account.password-change`, with nothing about either password.

get.summary: Where the signed-in venue user is signed in
get.description:
One row per admin-panel sign-in that can still carry on - a refresh chain neither revoked nor expired: `id`, `signedInAtUtc` (when the password was typed), `lastActiveAtUtc` (when it last renewed its access token, which a console in use does about every 15 minutes) and `isCurrent`, the sign-in this request's token belongs to. The current one first, then the most recently active.

**No device, browser or place**: nothing records them, so nothing here claims them.

post.summary: Sign the venue user out everywhere else
post.description:
Ends every other sign-in now: their refresh tokens are revoked and the session generation moves, so their access tokens are refused with `401 session-revoked` at once rather than when they expire. `endedSessions` counts the sign-ins that could still carry on and now cannot; 0 is an answer.

**This request's access token ends too, and its refresh token is kept**: refresh (`refreshVenueUserToken`) with the one you hold and carry on. No fresh pair is answered, on purpose - an access token alone must not be able to mint a new 30-day refresh token. **Audited** as `account.sign-out-others`.

A token that names no sign-in (no refresh-chain claim, from before the claim existed) cannot say which one to keep: `409 sign-in-unknown`, and nothing is changed - sign in again and retry.

get.summary: The venue you work in, with the branches your account covers
get.description:
The read the console opens a venue with. **Which branches come back is decided from the caller's own staff record, not from the token**: an owner covers every branch of the venue, whether or not their record names a home branch; a general manager covers every branch; a branch manager is given their own branch only - the only one the server lets them act on; a platform admin is given everything.

Branches are listed active first, then by name. An inactive branch is listed and flagged rather than hidden.

This is not `GET /api/platform/venues/{id}`, which is the platform tier's and refuses every venue user. Nothing here is platform-only: no tier rollup, no paid-branch count, no suspension timestamps.

put.summary: Set the published phone number, whether the page takes bookings, and the cover photo
put.description:
`acceptsWebBookings` is **false until somebody switches it on**, and stays false for every branch that has never been asked. A venue has not agreed to take bookings from strangers on the internet by never having been consulted, so this is a decision made during onboarding rather than a default inherited - which is also why it appears on the branch readiness checklist.

While it is off the public page still shows the room, the menu and the hours and simply offers no booking.

`phoneE164` must be E.164 (`+37411223344`); spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped first. Null or blank clears it. A branch with no number published is a branch a diner on the public page has no way to ask about a high chair.

`coverPhotoId` is the venue card's picture: a photo uploaded for **this** branch through `POST /api/branches/{branchId}/photos`, or null to clear it. A photo uploaded for another branch is not found here, and the whole form is refused before anything is written. The cover is the card's picture only - tables are pinned on room photos through the floor plan, so changing it moves no pin.

put.summary: Set cuisine, about, price level, website, amenities, district, map pin and gallery
put.description:
Every listing field is replaced; null or blank clears it. `priceLevel` is 1-4; `amenities` are keys from `outdoorSeating`, `wifi`, `parking`, `cardPayment`, `vegan`; `websiteUrl` is an absolute http(s) address; `district` is the part of town, e.g. `Kentron`, trimmed, at most 60 characters, and a manager may set it like any other listing field - it is not the address and moves nothing. Every broken field is reported at once as `422 validation-failed`.

**Moving the branch.** `address`, `latitude` and `longitude` travel together: coordinates without an address, or an address without coordinates, is `422` naming the missing field (bound `required`); the address is at most 400 characters. Sending all three as they are stored is not a move. A move - any of them present and different from the stored value - is allowed only to an **owner of this venue or a platform admin signed in to the admin panel**; anyone else (a manager, or any PIN session) gets `403 relocation-not-allowed` and **nothing on the form is saved**. A move is audited as `branch.relocate` with the old and new address and coordinates.

`galleryPhotoIds` are photos uploaded for **this** branch through `POST /api/branches/{branchId}/photos`, in display order, at most 12. **Null leaves the gallery alone**; `[]` clears it. A photo from another branch is 404 and nothing is written.

put.summary: Replace the reservation policy
put.description:
Every field, as one form. Out-of-range values are **refused, never clamped** - a turn time of 5 minutes or 12 hours gets a 422 that says so.

**Every refusal names its field.** `context.field` is the first offending property and `context.fields` is all of them, each with the `bound` it broke, the `min` and `max` allowed and the `value` sent - in the same casing this schema uses, so a form can put each message against its own input without mapping English prose back to a field. A request that breaks six bounds reports six.

**Existing bookings are never touched.** If the new window or turn time would not have allowed some of them, `affectedExistingReservations` says how many and `affectedReservationIds` which; they stay exactly as booked. The new rules apply to future bookings only.

get.summary: The console's Overview: today at this branch
get.description:
One read for the Overview screen's numbers. No parameters. Poll it with the approvals list and read it again after any booking action.

**Today is the branch's service day** (`serviceDate`), in its own time zone at `asOfUtc`: the calendar day at the branch (`localDate`, `localTime`), except while last night's opening block is still open past midnight - at 01:00 on Sunday a bar open 20:00-02:00 is still in Saturday's service. A booking belongs to the service day it starts in: 00:30 on Sunday inside Saturday's block is Saturday's, and 00:30 on Saturday was Friday night's. A block closing at 00:00 does not run past midnight.

- `graceMinutes`: how long past its start a late party's table is held (the policy's grace).
- `hours`: `isOpen`; while open `closesAt` and `closesNextDay` (the close falls after midnight tonight - "(next day)"; false for a 00:00 close, which reads "until 00:00", and for last night's block, which closes today); while shut `opensAt`, the next opening later today, absent when there is none.
- `bookings`: the service day's bookings - `total` (pending, confirmed, seated, completed and no-shows), `pendingApproval` (requests with no confirmed slot today to fall back to), `confirmed` (the late ones and the confirmed bookings whose change is waiting included), `late` (of those, start passed), `seated`, `completed`, `noShow`, `cancelled` (by the diner or the venue, declined requests included), `people` (the party sizes of the pending, confirmed, seated and completed) and `pendingChanges` (confirmed bookings with a change waiting).
- `inRoom`: `people` at the sittings still open, `occupiedTables`, `tables` (active, any state) and `outOfServiceTables`.
- `openTabs`: `count` open or settling and `unpaidAmd`, what they still owe.
- `revenue`: `todayAmd`, the closed tabs' totals from `sinceUtc` - the service date's first opening, or its local midnight when it has no hours - until now, against `lastWeekAmd` from the same opening on `lastWeekDate` (seven days before) for as long on the clock; `changePercent` to one decimal, absent when last week took nothing. A tab counts at the moment it closed.
- `load`: `capacity` (seats at the active tables in service - the chart's full-room line) and `hours`, one entry per hour **numbered from the service date's midnight**: 0-23 on that date, then 24 for 00:00-01:00 of the next, 25 for 01:00 - label one `hour % 24`. They run from the first opening (or booking) to the last open (or booked) hour. `people` are the confirmed, seated and completed parties whose sitting touches the hour, `pendingPeople` the unanswered requests and the slots changes ask for. Empty when shut all day with nothing booked.
- `todayBookings`: the service day's bookings by start, **leaving out the cancelled and declined**, at most 200 (`todayBookingsTruncated` when there were more; the counts and the chart read them all) - `id`, `code`, `status`, `startUtc`, `endUtc`, `localDate`, `localStartTime`, `partySize`, `guestName`, `tableId`, `tableLabel`, `tableStatus` (the table now), `roomName`, `channel`, `changeRequested`, `holdExpiresAtUtc` and `lateNudgeAtUtc`/`lateNudgeSent`. A confirmed booking whose change is waiting is listed at the slot still promised (its time, table and party) with `changeRequested` true and `status` 1 PendingApproval: the change is in the approvals list, and the floor's actions on it wait for that answer. `holdExpiresAtUtc` and the nudge are given only for a `Confirmed` booking; the nudge is the one the outbox holds - its send time once `lateNudgeSent`, else when it is due; there is no manual nudge. No guest phone numbers.

The row menu's actions are the floor's own routes, which the console's sign-in may call: `seat-reservation` and `free` under `/api/branches/{branchId}/tables/{tableId}`, and `no-show`, `release` (`outcome` 2 to cancel as the venue), `approve` and `reject` under `/api/reservations/{id}`.

At most seven statements however many bookings. An owner or general manager at any branch of their venue, a branch manager at their own branch only, a platform admin anywhere.

put.summary: Replace the rooms, their photos and every table's pin in one atomic call
put.description:
The editor sends the finished layout: rooms with their `photoIds`, and tables with their pins. It lands whole or not at all.

- Tables match by `id`, then by `label`, so an editor that lost the ids still edits the same tables and their **QR codes survive**. A QR token is never regenerated by an edit.
- Labels must be unique and present; room names too. Violations are `422 floor-plan-invalid` naming them in `context.errors`.
- A room has at most 10 photos (`areas[i].photoIds`, bound `max`), no photo twice, and a photo is in at most one room (`areas[i].photoIds[j]`, bound `conflict`). A photo not uploaded for this branch is `404`, the gallery's answer.
- A pin is `photoId`, `photoX` and `photoY` together or none of them (`tables[i].photoX`, bound `required`), each coordinate 0-1 (bound `range`), on one of **the table's own room's** photos (`tables[i].photoId`, bound `conflict`).
- **A photo dropped from every room takes its tables off it**: a table still sent pinned on such a photo is saved with no pin rather than refused.
- A bookable table with no pin is saved, with a warning: diners are not offered it.
- A table omitted from the plan is deleted only if it has never been used. One with any reservation, session or tab is **deactivated** instead, and `deactivatedTables` says so. One with a booking still to come (Confirmed or PendingApproval, not yet ended) is refused: `409 table-has-future-bookings` naming `context.tables` and `context.bookings`, nothing written.
- **`expectedVersion` is required**: the `version` the editor loaded. A plan saved by somebody else since then is `409 floor-plan-changed` with `context.currentVersion`, and nothing is written. Missing, it is `422` naming `expectedVersion`. A successful save returns the new `version`; nothing else moves it.

post.summary: Give an owner, general manager or branch manager their admin-panel sign-in
post.description:
Stores the address and returns a link the person opens to choose their own password. Nobody types a password for somebody else: the reset endpoint that consumes the link is the only thing that ever sets one.

The link is returned **once** and this is the only copy - the server keeps the token's hash and never logs it, so a lost link is replaced by issuing another. It is good for 24 hours and exactly one use. Issuing a new link retires any earlier unused one; two links issued at the same instant can both be live until one is used.

Only somebody the caller strictly outranks: a general manager issues for branch managers, an owner for general and branch managers, a platform admin for owners as well, and nobody for a peer or for themselves. A person who already has a password keeps it - and their open sessions - until the link is used, when both are replaced. Their sign-in address changes to the one given as soon as this answers.

Ten a minute per caller: this mints a credential, so it spends the sign-in budget rather than the global one.

get.summary: The branch's shifts over a window, and how many people are on shift today
get.description:
The minimal shift model: one person, one branch, one `date` (the branch's local date it starts on) with `startsAt` and `endsAt`, or `dayOff` with no times. `endsNextDay` when the end is at or before the start - overnight, including an end at exactly 00:00.

`serviceDate` is today at the branch, as on the Overview: its own date, or yesterday while last night's opening block still runs past midnight. `from` defaults to it and `to` to two weeks from `from`; at most 92 days (`to` `min` / `max` otherwise). `onShiftToday` counts the active people with a working shift here dated `serviceDate`. Only the shifts of active people who still work at this branch (theirs, or the whole venue) are listed, by date, then start (days off first).

An owner or general manager at any branch of their venue, a branch manager at their own, a platform admin anywhere.

post.summary: Plan a shift, or a day off, for one person
post.description:
`staffMemberId` must work at this branch (its own people, or an owner or general manager of the venue) and be active. The caller must be able to manage them - the staff edit's rank check: an owner anyone including a co-owner, a general manager branch managers, waiters and kitchen, a branch manager waiters and kitchen of their own branch only (not one who works the whole venue) - or be them. Times are whole minutes; seconds are dropped.

**Every refusal names its field**: `staffMemberId` `required`; `date` `required`, `min` (before the service date), `max` (more than 92 days after it) or `conflict` (a day off and anything else on one date for the person); `startsAt`/`endsAt` `required` for a working shift; `startsAt` `conflict` for times on a day off, or when it overlaps another of the person's shifts at any branch of the venue, compared as instants in each branch's zone (touching is fine); `endsAt` `conflict` (no length) or `max` (longer than 16 hours, `max` 960 minutes).

Writes for one person queue on their staff row, so two overlapping shifts saved at once cannot both land.

get.summary: This branch's reviews for moderation, with report counts
get.description:
Every review of the branch - published or hidden - with `hidden`, `hiddenReason`, `hiddenAtUtc`, `hiddenByPlatform`, `reportCount` and `lastReportedAtUtc`. `authorName` is the public name, never the account's full name, number or email. `hiddenByName` is the venue staff member who hid it (absent when shown, or when the platform hid it), and `reply` the venue's public reply (absent until there is one).

`summary` is the whole branch whatever the filter and page: `all`, `reported`, `hidden` and `visible` counts, `rating` (shown reviews, one decimal), `ratingChange30Days` (that minus the rating of the shown reviews written more than 30 days ago) and `distribution`, five rows of `{ stars, count }` from 5 down.

`filter`: `all` (default, newest written first), `reported` (at least one diner report, most recently reported first) or `hidden`. `page` from 1, `pageSize` 1-100 (default 20); `total` counts the rows for the filter.

Scoped like every branch setting: a manager whose account names a home branch reaches that branch only.

get.summary: How full the room was, and how long people actually stayed
get.description:
Tables occupied by hour of day and by weekday, seats filled against capacity, and walk-ins against bookings.

**`turnTime` is a distribution, not an average, and it is the most useful number in the whole set.** A cafe whose policy says 120 minutes and whose real median is 165 is refusing a 20:00 sitting because it believes the 18:00 one ends at 20:00 - and half the time it does not. It is losing bookings it has no other way to see. An average hides exactly that: a fast lunch and a slow dinner average to something plausible and describe neither service. Read `medianMinutes`, `p90Minutes` and `overPolicyFraction` together.

A sitting is counted in **every hour it spans**, not only the one it started in: "how busy is the room at eight" is a question about occupancy, and counting arrivals makes a restaurant look empty at its busiest hour.

`turnTime.buckets` are half-hour bars, `upToMinutes` 60 to 240 (each up to and including) and an open-ended last one. `walkInGuests` and `reservationGuests` split the people, not the sittings; `turnsPerTable` is sittings per active table per day (`activeTables`), two decimals, both periods over today's tables.

get.summary: Bookings, and what became of them
get.description:
Booked, seated, cancelled and no-show with their rates, late cancellations against the branch's own deadline, and how far ahead people book.

`leadTime` is what `bookingWindowDays` should be set from - a venue taking bookings 30 days out when nobody books more than 5 days ahead is holding tables against demand that does not exist. Its buckets are `upToHours` 2, 6, 24, 72, 168 and an open-ended last one, each **strictly less than** - a booking made exactly two hours ahead is in the 6.

**`webBookingsWithoutAnApp` is the number that decides a commercial question.** Somebody who booked from the public page and has no registered device cannot be reached by the reminder, the late nudge or one-tap cancel - the entire no-show story. If that number is large, an SMS or Telegram channel is worth paying for; if it is small, the install prompt on the confirmation screen is enough. See `docs/reports.md`.

get.summary: What was taken, by day and by hour
get.description:
Total, average tab and **average per head** - a different question from average tab, and the one a menu is priced against. Service charge collected, cash against in-app, and comps and discounts as their own line **with who authorised them**.

That last part is why adjustments are manager-only: an owner asking "what did we give away last month, and who decided" is asking both halves.

Revenue is counted on the tab **closing**, so a sitting that starts at 23:30 and settles at 00:40 belongs to the night it was taken - which is the day the venue counted its drawer.

`byDay` has one entry for every local date of the range, zero days included, and `previousByDay` the same for the previous equivalent period, so the two pair by index. `tabs` is the closed tabs with their comparison.

**Takeaway.** Orders collected at the counter are revenue too, counted when collected: `totalAmd` is `hallAmd` (the closed tabs, `tabs` of them) plus `takeawayAmd` (`takeawayOrders` of them); `byDay` carries each day's `takeawayAmd` and `takeawayOrders` inside its `revenueAmd`, and `byHour` puts an order in the hour it was collected. `cashAmd` includes the counter's cash and `cardAmd` its card payments, so cash + card + in-app is the total. `takeawayNotCollected` counts the orders marked not collected in the period. Average tab, per head and service charge stay the hall's. The CSV's day rows say `hallAmd` and `takeawayAmd` apart.

get.summary: The History: who did what at the branch, newest first
get.description:
Every recorded action - bookings, tables, orders, money, takeaway, guest messages, settings, the team and devices - with who did it (staff, the guest, or the system), from which device (`deviceLabel`: the tablet's name, "{first name}'s phone" for a personal phone, `Console` for the console), and what it was about.

Query, all optional: `date` (one branch-local day, `yyyy-MM-dd`) **or** `from`/`to` (inclusive; both default to today) - not both; at most 366 days, not before today - 1095 (money is kept three years, everything else one) and not after today + 366. `staffMemberId`: only what this person did. `actorKind`: `staff`, `guest`, `system` (what the system did by itself) or `platform`. `category`: `booking`, `table`, `order`, `payment`, `takeaway`, `message`, `settings`, `staff` or `device`. `q` (at most 60): the table (exact), the guest (contains), a code (`T-482` or `482`, or a booking's), or a dish (contains). `limit` 1 to 100, default 50. `cursor`: the page before's `nextCursor`. A bad value is **422 `validation-failed`** naming each in `context.fields`.

Answers `{ items, nextCursor, from, to }`, newest first then by id, so equal instants neither repeat nor skip across pages. Each item: `id`, `occurredAtUtc`, `local` (`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` on the branch's clock), `actorKind` (`staff`, `guest`, `system`, `platform`), `staffMemberId`, `actorName`, `deviceId`, `deviceLabel`, `category`, `action` (a stable code - the list is in `docs/activity.md`), `subjectType` and `subjectId` (the detail link: `reservation`, `tab`, `takeaway`, `menu-item`, `staff`, `branch`, `device`, `service-request`, `table`, `table-session`), `subjectCode`, `tableSessionId`, `tableLabel`, `guestName`, `itemNames`, `amountAmd`, `isMoney`, `before`/`after` (what changed, shape per action), `reason` (as typed), `summary` (the parameters to render the line from - never prose) and `seconds` (a call's claim, a reply, a booking decision).

Entries that name no branch (an owner's account) are on every branch's feed for the owner, the general manager and the platform, and on none for a branch manager.

Manager or above, scoped like the Reviews page: a branch manager reaches their own branch only, the owner and the general manager every branch of their venue, a platform admin any. Waiters and the kitchen: 403.

get.summary: Staff → Results: everybody's numbers over the dates, and the branch's
get.description:
Query: `from`, `to` - branch-local dates, inclusive; `from` defaults to `to`, `to` to today; at most 366 days, not before today - 1095 nor after today + 366. Bad values: 422 `validation-failed`.

**Whose a sale is.** A bill counts when it closes, as the revenue report counts it, and is split over the table's waiters in the proportion of the lines ordered while the table was theirs: a transfer moves what comes after it and leaves what came before. Tips are the waiter's whose table it was when paid; cash is whoever took it (the takeaway counter's included). A table and its guests count for each waiter with a share of the bill or holding it at the close.

Each row: `staffMemberId`, `name`, `role`, `isActive`, `tables`, `guests`, `salesAmd`, `averageCheckAmd`, `tipsAmd`, `callsClaimed` and `callClaimMedianSeconds` (call to "I'm on it"), `messagesAnswered` and `messageReplyMedianSeconds` (guest text to the first venue reply), `approvals`, `declines`, `cashAmd`, `cashPayments`, `discounts`, `comps`, `adjustmentsAmd`, `voids`. Medians are of whole seconds - the mean of the middle two for an even count, rounded half up; absent with none. Rows: everybody with anything in the window, and every active waiter and manager of the branch with nothing.

`totals` counts the branch once (a transferred table is one table; the medians are over every claim and reply). **Its money is the revenue report's for the same dates**: `salesAmd` = `hallAmd`, `tables` = `tabs`, `averageCheckAmd` = `averageTabAmd`, `cashAmd` = `cashAmd`, `takeawayAmd` = `takeawayAmd`, `adjustmentsAmd` = `adjustmentsTotalAmd`; `unattributedSalesAmd` is the part no waiter held.

Manager or above, scoped like the Reviews page: a branch manager reaches their own branch only, the owner and the general manager every branch of their venue, a platform admin any. Waiters and the kitchen: 403.

In Development the code comes back in `developmentCode`, so the flow works with no SMS provider wired up. That field is always null anywhere else.

post.summary: Exchange a one-time code for tokens
post.description:
Checks the newest live code for the number. On success the account is created if this is the first time - there is no separate registration step, because a separate registration step is a step people abandon.

**A registered number.** The account that registered with the number is signed in and its number marked verified; no second account is made. The first time, send the `Authorization: Bearer` token `register` returned: a request carrying that same account's token keeps its password and sessions. Without it - anonymous, or under a different diner - the code's holder is treated as the number's owner and the registrant as a stranger: the password is cleared (`hasPassword` false) and every refresh token for the account is revoked. The route stays anonymous; an invalid token is ignored, not refused.

A wrong code spends one of five attempts and says how many are left. The sixth attempt is refused outright with 429: the code is dead and a new one is needed.

**The phone number is stored as typed and is not verified by registering.** The account's `phoneVerified` stays false until a one-time code to it is passed once; the profile screen shows a *verify* link until then.

Username: 3-30 characters, letters, digits, dots and underscores, lowercased on the way in. Password: 8-128 characters and not the username or the email - no composition rules. A malformed field answers 400 with `context.field` naming it.

post.summary: Pair a personal phone with a code and the person's own PIN
post.description:
**A phone is a tablet that belongs to one person.** A manager issues a ten-minute, single-use code for somebody (`POST /api/branches/{branchId}/staff/{staffMemberId}/phone-pairings`), the phone scans it, and the person taps their own PIN. The answer is exactly what enrolling a tablet and then tapping a PIN would give: `device` is `enrolStaffDevice`'s body - keep `deviceToken` - and `session` is `signInStaffWithPin`'s, so the person is signed in.

From then on the phone's PIN screen lists only that person (`GET /api/auth/staff/roster`), `GET /api/auth/staff/device` says `kind: 2` and names them in `boundStaffMember`, and `POST /api/auth/staff/pin` accepts only their id - anybody else's is refused as a wrong PIN.

**The PIN** is checked with the lockout every PIN sign-in has: a wrong one is `401 pin-invalid` and counts toward the person's five; the fifth is `403 account-locked`. A wrong PIN leaves the code usable until it expires.

**The same browser again.** A live phone of this person's at the branch with the same `clientDeviceId` is reused (renamed to `deviceName`, its `platform` and `browser` replaced, a new device token). A live phone of somebody else's with it, or this person's at another branch, is unpaired - the browser holds one device token, and now it is this one. A live **tablet** with it is refused with `409` - a manager revokes the tablet first.

Kitchen staff cannot have a phone: `409 kitchen-phone-not-allowed`.

For the PIN screen. **A tablet on a counter should say where it thinks it is** - without this a browser enrolled months ago shows a keypad with no indication of which branch it will act on, and a laptop bound to the wrong one is first noticed in an audit row.

Authenticated by the device token. A revoked device is refused here too: showing a venue name and a keypad to somebody holding a killed tablet is the wrong answer twice.

`kind` is 1 for a tablet and 2 for a personal phone; a phone also carries `boundStaffMember` (`id`, `fullName`, `role`) - the one person whose PIN opens it.

M:Yalla.Api.Endpoints.AuthEndpoints.GetEnrolledDeviceAsync(Yalla.Application.Auth.IStaffAuthService,Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext,System.Threading.CancellationToken) does, so the two refuse the same callers the same way.
get.description:
For the PIN screen, so a first sign-in is a name to tap rather than a staff member id to type. Exactly the people `POST /api/auth/staff/pin` would accept here: active, of this device's venue, and either at this device's branch or at no particular branch. Sorted by name.

Each person also says whether they are on shift, so the screen can list those people first - an order left to the client, as is re-reading it on a screen left open. The shift is the one at this device's branch: the one running now (`onShiftNow`; last night's still running past midnight included), else the next to start within 12 hours, across midnight too. Its `startsAt` / `endsAt` (branch wall clock), `endsNextDay` and `startsAtUtc` / `endsAtUtc` read as on `GET /api/branches/{branchId}/shifts`, and are absent when there is none to report: every shift is over or more than 12 hours off, at another branch, or a day off.

`onShiftNow` is `startsAtUtc <= now < endsAtUtc` - decided on the instants, not the wall clock, so an hour a clock change repeats does not put an ended shift back on. Both instants are always present with a shift, so a screen can re-check it against its own clock and agree: a start in an hour the clocks skip is read on the clock from before the change (02:30 that night is 03:30 summer time), a time in a repeated hour as its first pass. Shifts never narrow the list: everybody the PIN exchange accepts is on it.

Nothing else per person - no phone, email or PIN state - because whoever holds the tablet can read it.

Authenticated by the device token, and refused exactly as `GET /api/auth/staff/device` refuses: no token, or a revoked device, is a 401.

On a personal phone the list is its own person alone, with their shift - the PIN exchange takes nobody else's there.

post.summary:
The one endpoint that reads a claim in the handler, because the device is the credential
being exchanged rather than something being authorised.
post.description:
The whole point of the staff model: **a waiter never types an email during a Friday rush**. The tablet signs in once and stays signed in; a person becomes present with four taps.

Send the device token as the bearer. The session token that comes back carries the staff member, their role and the tablet's branch, and lasts thirty minutes; the renewal handle keeps it alive while the tablet is in use and stops working after thirty minutes of inactivity.

PINs are per person, never shared. A shared PIN is faster and destroys the audit trail that answers 'who gave away my reserved table'.

**On a personal phone** (`kind` 2) only the phone's own person is accepted. Anybody else's `staffMemberId` is refused exactly as a wrong PIN is (`401 pin-invalid`), before their PIN is checked: nothing counts toward their lockout and nothing says whose PIN it was.

post.summary: Start proving a phone number through the Telegram bot
post.description:
Issues a challenge and a single-use deep link into the bot. Open `deepLinkUrl`; Telegram starts the bot, which asks the person to share their contact. Then poll `claim` with `challengeId` every `pollAfterMs` until it answers `verified`.

**The number never passes through the app.** Telegram hands the bot the number it verified when the account was created, and only the sender's own contact card counts - a forwarded card does not.

Send the `Authorization: Bearer` token `register` returned when verifying a registered number from the same app, exactly as for `verify-code`: the claim then keeps the password. Without it the registrant is displaced. The route stays anonymous; an invalid token is ignored.

Rate limited per address like `request-code`. Not mapped at all when the Telegram door is switched off in configuration.

post.summary: Poll a Telegram verification and, once verified, exchange it for tokens
post.description:
`pending` while the bot has not been handed the number; `verified` exactly once, with `signIn` set to **exactly what `verify-code` returns** - the account is created on a first number, a registered number's account is signed in and its number marked verified, with the same displacement rule - and `phoneE164`, the number Telegram handed over, so the app can show it without reading the profile. After that the challenge is spent.

Unknown, expired and spent challenges - and one started under a different account than the one claiming it - all answer **410 `telegram-verification-expired`**: start again. Links last five minutes; a verified challenge stays claimable for two more.

Rate limited per address by its own `auth-telegram-claim` policy, sized for one app polling as told.

post.summary: Scan the table's QR code: open a tab, or land on the one already open
post.description:
The flow the product lives on. Anyone - booked, phoned ahead, or in off the street - scans the code on the table and gets a token scoped to that table's tab, with **no account behind it**.

What happens depends on the table:
- **Free**: a session and a tab open, the scanner is the host, the table becomes Occupied.
- **Seated, no tab yet** (a party a waiter sat down, or from a booking): a tab opens on their session and the scanner is the host.
- **Already has a tab**: no second tab. The scanner is put on it as a *pending* participant until the host approves them. `outcome` says which case applied.
- **Out of service**: 409.

Two phones scanning a free table at the same moment produce exactly one tab; the loser lands pending on it. A double scan with the same `clientCommandId` returns the same tab with `wasReplay` set.

**Admission.** A tab this scan opens with no proved phone number behind it (no diner token, or one whose number was never proved) **waits for a waiter** - `tab.admission.status` 1, nobody orders until a waiter admits it - where the branch's `unverifiedScansNeedAdmission` is on, the default. Off, it is admitted at once (`admittedBecause` 5). A proved scanner's tab is admitted at once (2).

**After a waiter turned a scan away** the phone that opened it is refused at the branch for 30 minutes, and the table opens no tab by such a scan for 2 (joining a live tab there is not affected): `409 scan-turned-away`, `context.retryAfterUtc`. Say "ask a waiter".

401.description: No usable token was presented, or the one presented was rejected.

403.description: The caller is authenticated but not allowed to perform this action.

Also returned when this `clientCommandId` was used by a different device. `scan-turned-away`: a waiter just turned a scan away (`context.retryAfterUtc`). `feature-not-enabled` (`context.feature` 5 TableService, `context.branchId`): the platform has not allowed table service at the branch - every tab route answers it there.

Invitations last thirty minutes. A screenshot from last Tuesday gets 401.

post.summary: "I'm at my table": open the tab on your booked table with your booking code
post.description:
For a diner who booked through the app and is at their table: the booking code in place of the table's QR token. The code finds **the caller's own** booking, the booking names the table, and from there it is exactly `POST /api/tabs/open` - the same four cases, the same host and pending guests, the same `outcome`, the same response body.

**Whose.** Only a booking this diner account made opens anything. Somebody else's code answers `404 booking-not-found`, word for word what a code nobody holds gets: a code is read out at the door and proves nothing.

**When.** A `Confirmed` booking opens from the branch's walk-in holdback before its start - the moment the branch starts keeping the table back from walk-ins for it - until its end. Earlier is `409 booking-too-early` with `context.earliestUtc`; from `endUtc` on, `409 booking-ended`. Late is fine: until a waiter releases the table it is still theirs. A `Seated` booking opens whatever the time - the venue already put the party there. Pending-approval, cancelled and no-show bookings answer `409 booking-not-active`, with `context.status` saying which; a completed one, `booking-ended`.

**Whose sitting.** A booking opens only its own sitting. If the table still has another party's sitting open - one that is not this booking's - the answer is `409 booking-table-occupied` and nobody is put on that tab. On the booking's own sitting, a tab somebody else opened first (a friend who scanned) takes the booker on **approved**, with no host tap; the host stays host.

**Seating.** A free table is seated *as the booking*: the sitting names it and the booking becomes `Seated`, so the floor does not go on treating a party that is eating as one that has not arrived.

Case, spaces and dashes in the code do not matter. A double tap with the same `clientCommandId` returns the same tab with `wasReplay` set.

400.description: Missing device id or clientCommandId.

401.description: No usable token was presented, or the one presented was rejected.

403.description: `phone-not-verified`: the account registered with a number it has never proved. Send the diner through the code flow (`request-code`, `verify-code`) first; reading and cancelling bookings stay open meanwhile.

404.description: `booking-not-found`: none of the caller's bookings has that code. Somebody else's booking answers exactly the same.

409.description: `booking-too-early` (`context.earliestUtc` says when), `booking-ended`, or `booking-not-active` (`context.status` says why), or `booking-table-occupied` (another party is still seated there) - branch on the code. And, as on the scan, the table out of service, the tab there being settled, or this `clientCommandId` used by another device - those with no `context`.

get.summary: The tab, as this participant is allowed to see it
get.description:
Projected through the caller's own flags by one function, so every rule applies the same way everywhere:
- The caller's **own items and own subtotal are always present**, whatever the flags. Own means their own orders, a waiter's keyed in with `onBehalfOfParticipantId` for them, and the shared lines they were at the table for - and, only with `tableTotalVisible`, the `isTableAttributed` lines they were at the table for: a waiter's lines for nobody in particular can be the whole bill. `/shares` charges a part of those either way.
- The **table total and other people's items appear only with `canSeeTableTotal`**, and only once approved. When hidden they are **absent from the body** - not zero, not null - with `tableTotalVisible: false` beside the gap, so no client can render a hidden total as a free bill.
- A **pending** participant sees their own row and nothing else.
- **Nothing silently disappears.** A voided line stays in both arrays with `isVoided`, `voidReason` and `voidedAtUtc`, worth zero and counted toward no total; comps and discounts appear in `adjustments` with the reason the manager typed - all of them with `tableTotalVisible`, otherwise only those on the caller's own lines, because one off the whole tab or another person's dish is the table's money. A bill whose number drops with no visible cause is the fastest way to make somebody distrust the app, and a waiter then has to explain it at the table.

Menu prices are not part of this view and stay visible through the menu, so a guest without the total can always work out what their own order costs - and `serviceChargePercent` is on the response **for everyone**, hidden total or not, because the percentage is a fact about the venue rather than an aggregate.

`timeZoneId` is the branch's IANA zone: render every instant here in it and never in the device's. `maxSequence` is where the tab's event stream stands, so a client never has to call `/events` purely to find out.

get.summary: Which tables a branch can offer for one slot
get.description:
Every table in the branch pinned on a room photo - `photoId`, `photoX`, `photoY` - with its derived state at the requested time, whether it can be booked for this party - and if not, the one specific reason - and the window the diner may have. Assembled in a single query. Returns no guest names and no money. Omit date and time for 'now, at the branch'.

Each table also says what booking it takes: `isRequestable` when the guest with it before has to agree to leave in time first (the booking waits - `requiresApproval`), and `mustFreeByUtc`/`mustFreeByLocal` when a full sitting would run into its next booking - send that instant back as `acceptsFreeByUtc` once the diner agrees. The rules are the day slots' - see `getBranchDaySlots`.

`excludeReservationId` leaves one booking out of the answer as though it had never been made - the diner's own, while they change it, so the table they already hold reads as free to them. Every other booking still counts, and an id that is not a booking at this branch changes nothing. Anonymous like the rest of the read: booking ids are unguessable, and the answer says no more about the one left out than that its table is free.

get.summary: Which start times on one day have a table for this party
get.description:
Every quarter of an hour from 00:00 on `date` (`stepMinutes` is 15) whose whole sitting - the branch's turn time - fits one opening block, earliest first. A time the branch is shut for is **left out**, never struck. Each slot carries `time` (`HH:mm`, branch wall clock), `startUtc`, `isAvailable`, `isRequestable`, `requiresApproval`, `freeTableCount`, `requestableTableCount`, `mustFreeByUtc`/`mustFreeByLocal` and, when not available, `unavailableReason`.

**`isAvailable`** is true when at least one bookable table pinned on a photo of its room seats the party within the seat-overhang limit and the table's evening allows it - free outright (`freeTableCount`) or once the guest before agrees to leave in time (`requestableTableCount`; `isRequestable` when that is all there is, and `requiresApproval` with it). These are the single-slot read's own rules over the same rows, so a time listed here is one `availability?time=` offers exactly those tables at, and a struck time one it offers none at.

**The table's evening** - fixed rules, the ones a booking is judged by under the table's lock: refused from the previous booking's start until ninety minutes after it (`TableJustBooked` 11) and within forty-five minutes before the next one (`NextBookingTooSoon` 12); from ninety minutes to three hours after the previous start, or while that sitting plus clearing time still runs, the table can only be asked for - its guest is asked to have left by the start less the clearing time - and while one such question to a guest is open nobody else can ask (`EarlierGuestBeingAsked` 13). A sitting that would run into the next booking ends at that booking's start less the clearing time; `mustFreeByUtc` is the latest such time when no table on offer gives a full sitting.

**Why a time is struck**: `LeadTimeTooShort` (1) or `OutsideBookingWindow` (2) when the time itself is refused; otherwise, when tables that fit the party are taken, the commonest of `TableAlreadyBooked` (8), `TableCurrentlyOccupied` (10), `TableJustBooked` (11), `NextBookingTooSoon` (12) and `EarlierGuestBeingAsked` (13); else the commonest table reason, e.g. `PartyExceedsCapacity` (4) when nothing seats them.

The top-level `unavailableReason` refuses the whole day: `OutsideOpeningHours` (3) with no slots when the branch is shut all day, or the timing reason every listed time shares - a past day, the rest of today inside the lead time, a date beyond the booking window. Null when any time was judged on its tables.

One query, like the single slot. Returns no guest names and no money. `partySize` defaults to 2.

`excludeReservationId` leaves one booking out of the answer as though it had never been made - the diner's own, while they change it, so the table they already hold reads as free to them. Every other booking still counts, and an id that is not a booking at this branch changes nothing. Anonymous like the rest of the read: booking ids are unguessable, and the answer says no more about the one left out than that its table is free.

So it needs web bookings allowed by the platform (`409 feature-not-enabled`, `context.feature` 2) and the venue's online bookings switched on (`409 web-bookings-not-accepted`); the reservation policy need not have been saved, as the app's must. The diner is the one the code flow signed in (a proved number, as for `createReservation`).

**Sold-out items are returned with `isAvailable: false`, not hidden.** A dish that silently vanishes looks like a broken menu and sends the diner to ask a waiter - the exact question this feature exists to remove. Grey it out and keep the price.

**Unfinished items are excluded entirely, which is the opposite rule for the opposite reason.** Since the photo requirement moved from create-time to go-live-time an item can exist without a photo, a description, ingredients, allergens, a portion size or a prep time - that is how a menu gets typed in before it gets photographed - and none of those may reach a diner. Somebody reading an empty allergen list reasonably concludes there are none.

So every descriptive field on this read is always present and `isComplete` is always true. The console's `GET /api/branches/{branchId}/menu/manage` is where the unfinished ones are visible.

post.summary: Ask a waiter for something
post.description:
Presets and one short optional note. **Not a chat**: a message box creates the expectation of a reply, and during the Friday rush nobody answers it.

Rate limited **per tab**, not per person - the list a waiter is looking at is the table's, and one bored guest must not be able to bury another table's request.

**Asking for the bill from the pay sheet.** With `preset` 3 a request may carry `billScope` (1 WholeBill, 2 MyShare) and `tipPercent` (0 to 25). The server prices it from the tab's own arithmetic - the same numbers `/shares` reports - and the response and the waiter's list carry `billAmountAmd` and `tipAmd`:
- WholeBill: the tab's remaining balance. Only for somebody who can see the table total - otherwise 403.
- MyShare: what the asker still owes of their own share (`shareAmd` less `paidAmd`); for somebody who can see the table total, never more than the tab owes.

The tip is on the **unpaid part of the items**: the tab subtotal (WholeBill) or the asker's `personalAmd` (MyShare), in the proportion `billAmountAmd` bears to the total or the share - all of the items when nothing has been paid. The service charge is inside `billAmountAmd`; the tip is **outside** it, as a cash payment's `tipAmd` is outside the balance. Either field on another preset, a tip with no scope, or a tip outside 0 to 25 is a 422 naming the field; a scope with nothing left to pay is a 422 on `billScope`.

A request with a `billScope` **replaces** the asker's own earlier open request for the bill on this tab: that one leaves the waiter's list. The `ServiceRequested` event carries `billScope` and `tipPercent` but never the amounts - every phone at the table reads the stream.

Proof first: `password` when the account has one (`hasPassword`), otherwise `code` - a one-time code from `POST /api/auth/diner/request-code` for the account's own number - or **nothing, from a session that proved the phone in the last ten minutes** (a Telegram or code sign-in; the token's `phone_proved_at`). **In one transaction**: the account becomes a tombstone - number, username, email, name, password and verification stamp cleared, so all three can register again; every session ends (access and refresh tokens); push devices, every review by the account and its pictures (files included) are deleted. The venue keeps its records with the link to the person removed: bookings keep the guest name and number typed into them, places at a table become `Guest`, orders stay. An audit row `diner.delete` is written.

**Forgot it?** Sign in again with a code (`verify-code`) or the Telegram bot: for ten minutes after that sign-in, `currentPassword` may be left out. Past that, or from a password sign-in or a refreshed token, leaving it out is `422 validation-failed` with `context.field` = `currentPassword`.

The new password is under the same rule as registration: 8-128 characters, and not the username or the email.

**Every access token the account holds ends, this one included**: the next call with it answers `401 session-revoked`. **Every other sign-in's refresh token is revoked**, so other devices are signed out; the sign-in this token came from keeps its refresh token, so the app refreshes and carries on.

Replaces whatever picture was there. The same bytes uploaded twice by the same person are one photo. The picture replaced is left for the orphan sweep, which runs every hour by default (`PhotoStorage:SweepIntervalMinutes`) and deletes a picture nothing uses once it is more than a day old - so its old URL keeps working for at least a day and stops within about an hour after that. To end it at once, `DELETE /api/diner/me/photo` before uploading.

post.summary: Book a table
post.description:
**The diner app's booking route.** It books on the `App` channel whatever the body says: `channel` is deprecated and ignored (the public page books through `createPublicReservation`). So it needs app bookings allowed by the platform (`409 feature-not-enabled`, `context.feature` 1) and, the venue's own gate, online bookings switched on with the reservation policy saved (`409 bookings-not-accepted`).

Idempotent on `clientCommandId`: a retry returns the original booking and creates nothing, answering 200 rather than 201. Lands as `Confirmed`, or `PendingApproval` (`awaitingApprovalBecause` says why) when the booking is at **short notice** - for the branch's today, or starting under six hours from now - the branch approves every booking, the party is over the branch's threshold, or the diner is over the rolling no-show threshold.

A short-notice booking (`awaitingApprovalBecause` 4) is the floor's to decide, by `approvalExpiresAtUtc` - fifteen minutes from now, or the start if sooner. Unanswered by then it is declined (`CancelledByVenue`, `declinedBecause` 2 NoAnswer) and the diner gets a `reservation-decided` push with `expired` true. Count down to `approvalExpiresAtUtc`; read the booking again to see the answer.

A booking for a table whose previous booking started under three hours before (`awaitingApprovalBecause` 5 EarlierGuestConsent) waits on that guest's yes, for **two hours** at most (`approvalExpiresAtUtc`, never past their start nor this one's). When `awaitsEarlierGuestAnswer` is true they are asked in the app and only they answer - unanswered it is declined with `declinedBecause` 4 EarlierGuestNoAnswer. When it is false the floor calls them and decides, by the same deadline - unanswered it is declined with `declinedBecause` 2 NoAnswer.

**Only an account whose number is proved books** (`403 phone-not-verified` otherwise - send the diner to verify it). **At most three active bookings per proved number**, at every venue: the fourth is `409 phone-has-active-booking` with `context.maxActiveBookings` and the diner's own earliest active booking (`reservationId`, `code`, `startUtc`, `localDate`, `localStartTime`, `venueName`, `branchName`). **A guest blocked for no-shows** (three in three days) is `403 booking-blocked-no-shows` with `context.blockedUntilUtc` until the block ends.

With `autoConfirmGuestsWithGoodRecord` on at a branch that approves every booking, a guest with a good record is confirmed at once - see `GET /api/branches/{id}/reservation-policy`.

**One table at a time per diner, anywhere**: a sitting that overlaps another of the diner's own live bookings (pending, confirmed or seated) is `409 reservation-overlaps-own`, with `context` naming the booking already held - `reservationId`, `code` (its door code), `localDate` (`"2026-10-22"`, the branch's calendar - say the day when it differs), `localStartTime` (`"19:30:00"`), `tableLabel`, `venueName` and `branchName` - so the app can say "You already have a booking at Café Aram at 19:30". At the same branch sittings that only touch do not overlap; at **another venue** the two need **30 minutes** between them (with a 90-minute sitting, starts less than 2 hours apart are refused). A retry with the same `clientCommandId` still answers as a replay.

post.summary: Change a booking's date, time, party size or table
post.description:
Moves the diner's **own** booking and answers with it: the **same `id` and `code`** and manage link, at the new `startUtc`/`endUtc`, `partySize`, `tableId`, `roomId`/`roomName` and `status`. Send the whole new slot - `date`, `time`, `partySize` and `diningTableId` (required, the current table or another at the branch) - as a new booking would.

**Only a booking still to come**: `PendingApproval` or `Confirmed` and not yet started. Anything else - seated, finished, cancelled, a no-show, or past its start - is `409 reservation-not-changeable`, before the new slot is looked at.

**Judged as a new booking would be**, with the same `reservation-*` 422s: the branch open for business and still taking bookings from the channel the booking came from, lead time and booking window, opening hours, the table pinned on its room and fitting the party. The clash check runs under the target table's lock **excluding this booking**, so moving dinner by half an hour on the same table is never refused because of itself - and the 409's fresh floor shows the diner's own table free.

**The status is decided again** by the create rules: the move can keep it `Confirmed`, confirm a pending one, or send it back to `PendingApproval` (`awaitingApprovalBecause` says why). A `Confirmed` booking that keeps its **table and start** and does not grow stays `Confirmed`, today included - nothing about it got harder to keep. Otherwise a move into the short-notice window (today, or under six hours away) goes to `PendingApproval` with a fifteen-minute `approvalExpiresAtUtc` - and keeps the slot it had: if the change is declined, or nobody answers it, the booking goes back to that slot, `Confirmed` as before, when it is still free. A booking **already waiting** on a short-notice answer keeps its deadline through a move (never past the new start); past the deadline it cannot be moved at all - `409 reservation-approval-expired`. A `Confirmed` booking whose party does not grow keeps its confirmation against the party-size threshold - the venue already said yes to that many people - but not against a branch that approves every booking or the diner's no-show history. A booking waiting on the guest before it (`awaitingApprovalBecause` 5) keeps its two-hour deadline through a move in the same way, whoever answers - the floor or that guest in the app.

**One table at a time per diner, anywhere**: a sitting that overlaps another of the diner's own live bookings (pending, confirmed or seated) is `409 reservation-overlaps-own`, with `context` naming the booking already held - `reservationId`, `code` (its door code), `localDate` (`"2026-10-22"`, the branch's calendar - say the day when it differs), `localStartTime` (`"19:30:00"`), `tableLabel`, `venueName` and `branchName` - so the app can say "You already have a booking at Café Aram at 19:30". At the same branch sittings that only touch do not overlap; at **another venue** the two need **30 minutes** between them (with a 90-minute sitting, starts less than 2 hours apart are refused). A retry with the same `clientCommandId` still answers as a replay. The booking being moved is left out of that check, and a change that keeps its table, start and end (a party size) is not judged by it.

The reminder and late nudge are replaced with ones for the new time. Idempotent on `clientCommandId`: a retry of the same change answers `200` with the booking **as it stands now** and `wasReplay: true`, moving nothing; the same id on another command, or on a different change (another table, start or party size), is `409 client-command-id-in-use` - mint a fresh id per change.

Never retried automatically: this answer will not change on a repeat. `reservation-overlaps-own`: another of the diner's bookings at this branch runs then - `context.reservationId`, `code`, `localDate`, `localStartTime`, `tableLabel` name it. `concurrent-update`: the booking was cancelled, approved or seated while this was in flight; read it again. `bookings-not-accepted`, `web-bookings-not-accepted`, `branch-unavailable`: the branch stopped taking bookings. `client-command-id-in-use`: the id belongs to another command or to a different change.

post.summary: Answer a later guest's request for your table: will you have left in time?
post.description:
Somebody would like the table after the diner's **own** booking - its `incomingTableRequest` says when (`requestedStartUtc`) and by when the diner is asked to have left (`freeByUtc`, the requested start less the branch's clearing time); the push is kind `table-request` with `reservationId` and `requestId`. The other guest stays anonymous.

`accept: true`: the later booking is confirmed, and this booking promises to free the table by `freeByUtc` - its `endUtc` is cut to it and `promisedFreeByUtc` set. `accept: false`: the later booking is declined (`declinedBecause` 3). Both diners are told. Answers with this booking as it now stands.

Before `expiresAtUtc` only - two hours from the request, never past this booking's start; unanswered by then the later booking is declined for it (`declinedBecause` 4) and this one is unchanged. Idempotent on `clientCommandId`, and the same answer twice is answered with the booking; a request answered the other way, expired, or withdrawn because either booking moved or ended is `409 table-request-not-pending`.

post.summary: Keep the table a little longer - the late nudge's action
post.description:
What the **late nudge** notification's action button calls. The diner taps it from the lock screen; they never open a screen and hunt for it.

**Once.** `graceExtensionsUsed` enforces it, and a second attempt is refused with a reason a diner can read. Repeated requests for five more minutes are how a table stays held all evening for somebody who is not coming.

The extension goes onto the branch change sequence, so the waiter watching that table sees it immediately rather than in a column nothing reads.

**Not before the booking starts.** Nothing is held until then, so there is nothing to keep: offer the button from the late nudge, or once `startUtc` has passed. A tap days early used to spend the one extension and ping the floor about a table nobody was holding.

get.description: `enabled` false: the venue does not take takeaway - no button. `open`: orders are taken now - inside today's opening hours and before closing minus the venue's last-order minutes. Open: `asapReadyAtUtc` / `asapReadyAt` (now plus `prepMinutes`), `slots` (quarter hours from then to `lastPickupAt`, as local `HH:mm`; a time that would put more orders in the kitchen than the venue allows is left out) and `busy` (the kitchen is full: "as soon as possible" is refused, a slot may still work). Closed: `opensAt` / `opensAtUtc` - the next opening an order can be taken from, within a week ("Takeaway from opening, 10:00"). Read it again when the checkout opens: slots move with the clock.

post.summary: Order to take away
post.description:
`pickup` is `{ "asap": true }` or `{ "at": "19:15" }` - one of the availability's `slots`. `lines` 1 to 30, `quantity` 1 to 20, at most 60 dishes in all; `note` at most 500 characters. Names and prices are taken as they stand now. **Idempotent on `clientCommandId`**: a retry answers the order the first try made, `wasReplay: true`.

A proved phone is required (403 `phone-not-verified`, as for booking). Refusals, before anything is saved: 422 `validation-failed` naming `lines`, `lines[i].quantity`, `note`, `pickup` or `pickup.at`; 409 `takeaway-not-accepted`; 409 `takeaway-closed` (`context.opensAtUtc`, `opensAt`); 409 `takeaway-busy` (ASAP while the kitchen is full - `context.maxInProgress`); 409 `takeaway-slot-unavailable` (`context.slots`: the ones on offer now); 422 `takeaway-items-unavailable` (`context.items[]` = `{ menuItemId, reason }`: 1 NotOnMenu, 2 SoldOut, 3 NotForTakeaway - every one); 409 `client-command-id-in-use`.

The order is `Sent` with `acceptDeadlineUtc` five minutes on - accepted on the tablet, or declined for nobody answering and the guest told. A branch that accepts automatically answers `Accepted` at once, ready when asked for. The code (`T-482`) is what the guest says at the counter.

`status`: 1 Sent (waiting for the venue; the guest may cancel), 2 Accepted ("Accepted · being prepared" - in the kitchen, ready at `readyAtUtc`), 3 Ready (waiting at the counter), 4 Collected (handed over and paid), 5 Declined (`declinedBecause` 1 the venue said no - `declineReason` when it said why - or 2 nobody answered within five minutes), 6 Cancelled (by the guest, while sent), 7 NoShow (ready, and nobody came within thirty minutes). Local times are `HH:mm` on the branch's wall clock.

get.summary: The booking's thread with the venue
get.description:
The caller's own booking only - anybody else's is 404, as is a thread that closed over 30 days ago. Nobody has written yet: `conversationId` absent and `messages` empty - the composer still shows while `open` and `guestsCanWrite`. The venue's side is the venue: no staff names here. `pendingAsk`: the venue asked "are you coming?", nobody answered since and the answer is still taken - show the answer bar (Coming / Late 10-15-30 / Not coming), which calls `confirmOnMyWay`, `reportRunningLate` and the booking's cancel. `venueLastReadUtc`: a guest message not after it is "seen". `unreadCount`: venue messages since the guest last read - mark read on open (`.../conversation/read`). post.summary: Order from your own phone
post.description:
Names and prices are **snapshotted onto every line** as they stand now, so a menu edit next week cannot change a bill presented tonight.

A `isShared` line records **who is at the table at this moment**: a friend who joins ten minutes later is not on the bottle, and one who is removed still is - they were there when it was poured.

An unavailable item refuses the **whole** order, by name, rather than quietly dropping it: a partial order is a decision made on your behalf that you discover when the food arrives.

`estimatedReadyAtUtc` comes from the longest prep time on the order, not the sum - a kitchen cooks an order together.

`totals` is the tab's, so it follows `tableTotalVisible` on your tab: **absent**, with `tableTotalVisible: false` beside it, when the host hid the total from you. Read it as optional.

`onBehalfOfParticipantId` and a line's `participantId` are the waiter's: a phone sending either is refused with 403 `forbidden`, its own id included.

get.summary: Who owes what
get.description:
Every split is integer and every remainder goes to the host, so the shares sum to the total **to the dram** - a property test asserts it over randomised tabs. Service charge splits pro rata: order 30% of the food, pay 30% of the service.

Without `canSeeTableTotal` you get **your own share and no table aggregate** - the members are absent from the body, not zeroed, so a hidden total cannot be rendered as a free bill.

A removed participant's items stay on the bill and fall to the host, reported in `absorbedFromRemovedAmd` rather than folded in silently.

get.summary: Catch up on what happened
get.description:
Everything after `afterSequence`, oldest first, for the phone that was in a lift when the wine was ordered.

`sequence` is this event's place **on this tab**, counting from 1, and the order is the order things happened - a payment that settles the bill is immediately followed by the close, never the other way round. Keep the highest you have seen and ask for everything after it.

**Ignore a `type` you do not recognise and keep your position**: new types will be added and an old build must not break on a tab that used one.

**You read the stream you may see.** Every event is here - the sequence never has a hole - but without `tableTotalVisible` on your tab the payloads carry only your own money: `orderPlaced.lines` holds just your lines (your own, a waiter's on your behalf, and shared items you were at the table for - never a waiter's line for the table, which can be the whole bill), a void names only your own dish, an adjustment says what, how much and why only when it is off your line, a payment says how much only when it was yours, and `remainingAmd`, `totalAmd` and `writtenOffAmd` are never there. While you wait for the host, other people's `displayName` and `note` are left out too. Redacted members are **absent**, never null or zero. See `docs/tabs.md`, section 7.4.

post.description:
**One review per diner per branch.** A second POST is `409 conflicting-state`; change the review with PUT instead.

**Needs a verified phone number** - `403 phone-not-verified` otherwise - **and a visit**: a booking of this diner's at the branch that was Seated or Completed, or a place on one of its tabs, in the last 180 days. Without one, `403 review-needs-visit` with `context.windowDays`.

`rating` 1-5 and `text` at most 1000 characters are `422 validation-failed` with `context.fields` naming each. The branch's `rating` and `reviewCount` on the list routes follow within fifteen seconds; the reviews route reads them live.

get.summary: The diner's orders, for the Orders tab
get.description:
Every order this diner is on: placed from their phone, keyed in by a waiter on their behalf, or keyed in for the whole table on a tab they were approved onto - and their takeaway orders (`kind: takeaway`). **Active ones first**, then newest first, at most 100.

`status=active` is New, InKitchen and Ready; `status=history` is Served and Voided; absent is both. Anything else is `400`.

`status` on each order is the app's word: New `confirmed`, InKitchen `preparing`, Ready `ready`, Served `completed`, Voided `cancelled`. `kind` is `dineIn` or `takeaway`. A dine-in `timeline` starts with `confirmed` at `placedAtUtc` and adds each kitchen step as it was recorded; `canCancel` is false - voiding an order is a staff action.

**Takeaway** (`kind: takeaway`): `tabId` absent, `tableLabel` empty, `partySize` 0; `status` is `inProgress` while it waits for the venue (Sent), `preparing` (Accepted), `ready`, `completed` (Collected) or `cancelled` (Declined, Cancelled or NoShow); `takeaway` carries the code, the exact status (1 Sent ... 7 NoShow), the pickup and ready times and the item count; `estimatedReadyAtUtc` is the ready time; `timeline` starts with `inProgress` at `placedAtUtc`; `canCancel` is true while Sent. Active for takeaway is Sent, Accepted and Ready. The whole order is `getDinerTakeawayOrder`.
