get.summary:
The day's slots, through the same read model as the app's - the public gate first, exactly as
for one slot.
get.description:
The app's day-slots read, reused rather than reimplemented, behind the public 404 rule and the tighter rate limit. `partySize` is required here, as on the public single-slot read.

Every quarter of an hour from 00:00 on `date` (`stepMinutes` is 15) whose whole sitting - the branch's turn time - fits one opening block, earliest first. A time the branch is shut for is **left out**, never struck. Each slot carries `time` (`HH:mm`, branch wall clock), `startUtc`, `isAvailable`, `isRequestable`, `requiresApproval`, `freeTableCount`, `requestableTableCount`, `mustFreeByUtc`/`mustFreeByLocal` and, when not available, `unavailableReason`.

**`isAvailable`** is true when at least one bookable table pinned on a photo of its room seats the party within the seat-overhang limit and the table's evening allows it - free outright (`freeTableCount`) or once the guest before agrees to leave in time (`requestableTableCount`; `isRequestable` when that is all there is, and `requiresApproval` with it). These are the single-slot read's own rules over the same rows, so a time listed here is one `availability?time=` offers exactly those tables at, and a struck time one it offers none at.

**The table's evening** - fixed rules, the ones a booking is judged by under the table's lock: refused from the previous booking's start until ninety minutes after it (`TableJustBooked` 11) and within forty-five minutes before the next one (`NextBookingTooSoon` 12); from ninety minutes to three hours after the previous start, or while that sitting plus clearing time still runs, the table can only be asked for - its guest is asked to have left by the start less the clearing time - and while one such question to a guest is open nobody else can ask (`EarlierGuestBeingAsked` 13). A sitting that would run into the next booking ends at that booking's start less the clearing time; `mustFreeByUtc` is the latest such time when no table on offer gives a full sitting.

**Why a time is struck**: `LeadTimeTooShort` (1) or `OutsideBookingWindow` (2) when the time itself is refused; otherwise, when tables that fit the party are taken, the commonest of `TableAlreadyBooked` (8), `TableCurrentlyOccupied` (10), `TableJustBooked` (11), `NextBookingTooSoon` (12) and `EarlierGuestBeingAsked` (13); else the commonest table reason, e.g. `PartyExceedsCapacity` (4) when nothing seats them.

The top-level `unavailableReason` refuses the whole day: `OutsideOpeningHours` (3) with no slots when the branch is shut all day, or the timing reason every listed time shares - a past day, the rest of today inside the lead time, a date beyond the booking window. Null when any time was judged on its tables.

One query, like the single slot. Returns no guest names and no money. `partySize` defaults to 2.

`excludeReservationId` leaves one booking out of the answer as though it had never been made - the diner's own, while they change it, so the table they already hold reads as free to them. Every other booking still counts, and an id that is not a booking at this branch changes nothing. Anonymous like the rest of the read: booking ids are unguessable, and the answer says no more about the one left out than that its table is free.

get.summary: One booking, by the manage link that was mailed with it
get.description:
What the confirmation screen renders, for somebody holding nothing but the link: venue, branch, address, table and the room it is in (`roomName`, absent for a table in no room), local date and time, party size, status, the code quoted at the door, and the instant past which cancelling counts as late. A waiting booking carries `approvalExpiresAtUtc` to count down to and `awaitsEarlierGuestAnswer`: true while the guest with the table before it is asked in the app whether they will have left in time (only they answer), false when the venue decides it.

For the page around it: `venueSlug` and `branchSlug`, the branch page's public address (`/{venueSlug}/{branchSlug}`) - the link a reminder carries is the web's token-only `/booking/{token}`, which names no branch - and, for changing the booking, `reservationId` (send it as `excludeReservationId` on the public availability and day-slot reads, so the table already held reads as free) and `tableId`, the booked table.

**Nothing else.** No diner id, no phone number, no other bookings, no floor state. The token is the whole credential and it will be pasted into WhatsApp, left in browser history and read by whoever picks the phone up, so this response is a hand-picked subset rather than a trimmed reservation.

**A cancelled, missed or finished booking answers 200 with its state**, not 404. Somebody opening a three-week-old link should learn what happened to their table.

**An unknown token, an expired one and a booking that no longer exists answer identically** - same status, same code, same sentence. The link must not be usable to find out which tokens are real. The link stops working `ManageTokenGraceDays` after the booking ends.

post.summary: Undo a soft delete
post.description:
The venue comes back exactly as it was before it was deleted: switched on or off as it was then, and **still suspended if it was suspended** - deleting never touched the suspension. Nothing under it was removed, so nothing is rebuilt; its branches, tables, staff and history are all where they were, and it accepts changes again. A venue deleted before this was recorded comes back switched off, for somebody to switch on on purpose.

A venue that is not deleted is answered as it is and nothing is written, so an undo that arrives twice is harmless. Refused with **409** when its web address now belongs to another venue - which the unique slug index, covering deleted venues, keeps from happening today. **Audited** as `venue.restore`.

post.summary: Change the signed-in platform admin's password
post.description:
`currentPassword` must be right and `newPassword` at least 12 characters - the one rule every console password follows. Everything wrong is reported in one 422: a wrong current password is `context.fields` naming `currentPassword`, not a 401, so the console stays signed in and shows it under the field.

**Answers a fresh token pair - store it.** The change ends every session the account has, at once: the session generation moves, so every admin-panel access token it holds - the one this request was sent with included - is refused from now on with `401 session-revoked`, every refresh token is revoked and every unused reset link is spent. The body (`accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresInSeconds`, the refresh endpoint's shape) is how the sign-in that made the change carries on.

**Wrong current passwords are counted per account**: each is audited as `admin.password-change-failed`, and after 10 inside 15 minutes the route answers `429 too-many-attempts` with `Retry-After` (and `context.retryAfterSeconds`) until the oldest leaves the window - right password or not. A successful change starts the count again. The route is also under the `auth` rate limit. The seed never resets a password changed here. **Audited** as `admin.password-change`, with nothing about either password.

post.summary: Staff: let a table that scanned without a verified number order
post.description:
A tab opened by a QR scan whose host has no proved phone number waits for a waiter (`admission.status` 1): the phones can read the menu and the tab, approve joiners and call a waiter, but not order. A waiter who can see the party at the table taps Admit; from then on it is an ordinary tab (approved guests with `canOrder` order, a phone's order waits at New for a waiter). A tab whose host proved their number, one opened from a booking, and one staff opened are admitted on the spot - and every scan is, at a branch whose policy has `unverifiedScansNeedAdmission` off. **A waiter's own order never admits a tab**: staff may order on a waiting tab, and it goes on waiting until this tap.

Already admitted answers `200` as it is, writing nothing. Two waiters tapping Admit and Reject on one card at once: one wins, the other gets `409 tab-admission-decided`. Writes `TabAdmitted` (21) on the tab's stream and a signal entry (2) on the branch's change stream. Idempotent on `clientCommandId`. **Online only** - not one of the commands the tablet queues.

post.summary: Staff: turn away a tab nobody is really sitting at
post.description:
For a tab waiting for admission that the waiter cannot match to anybody at the table - a photographed QR code scanned from somewhere else. The tab closes (`status` 3, `admission.status` 3), its live invitation is revoked and its open calls are acknowledged by the rejecting waiter.

**When the scan itself seated the table** (a walk-in sitting no waiter and no booking opened), the table is **freed** through the table state machine - an Occupied-to-Free audit row with the reason given - and `admission.tableFreed` is true. A table a waiter or a booking seated stays seated; only the tab goes, and the party really there can scan again for a new one. A scan that took a table **held** for a late booked party gives it back to Held, not Free.

**Afterwards, a pause:** the phone that opened the tab opens or joins no tab at the branch for 30 minutes, and the table opens no tab by an unverified scan for 2 (`409 scan-turned-away` on the scan, with `context.retryAfterUtc`); a waiter can open the tab for a party really there meanwhile. A tab a waiter has keyed orders on cannot be turned away (`409 conflicting-state`): move the host or remove the phone, then admit.

Already turned away answers `200` as it is; racing an Admit, the loser gets `409 tab-admission-decided`. Writes `TabAdmissionRejected` (22) on the tab's stream and a signal entry (3) on the branch's change stream. Idempotent on `clientCommandId`. **Online only.**

The floor (`getBranchFloor`) carries the badge too - poll this when the tab is open. Waiter or above at the branch.

post.description:
A waiter or above at the booking's own branch - an owner or general manager at any branch of their venue, a platform admin anywhere. Staff of one branch cannot decide another's bookings by guessing an id.

A short-notice booking (`awaitingApprovalBecause` 4) can be approved until `approvalExpiresAtUtc`, and no booking once it has started. The caller's **stored** role counts, not only the token's: a waiter moved to the kitchen is refused at once. A platform admin gets the booking back with `guestPhone` empty.

Drop the request from the panel: the diner is told the venue did not answer in time. `conflicting-state`: the booking is not waiting for approval. `reservation-cancelled-by-block` (`context.reservationId`, `cancelledAtUtc`): a no-show block cancelled it - its guest missed three bookings in three days. `reservation-awaiting-earlier-guest`: the booking waits on the guest before it on the table to answer in the app - theirs to answer, not the floor's (`context`: `reservationId`, `requestId`, `expiresAtUtc`). `table-request-not-pending`: approving a booking whose guest before has moved since they were asked.

post.description:
Scoped as `approve`. Refuses a booking that was already confirmed: the diner has been told it is theirs. `reason` is optional and recorded as `cancellationReason`; the booking answers `declinedBecause` 1 (StaffDeclined). A short-notice booking can be declined until `approvalExpiresAtUtc` - after that it is declined for nobody answering, and the diner is told that instead.

**A change of a confirmed booking** is declined as a change: when the slot it had is still free the answer is the booking back there - `Confirmed`, its old `startUtc`, `tableId` and `partySize` - and the diner is told it stands (`reservation-decided` with `wasChange` and `originalKept` "true"); when that slot has gone too it is declined as above, with `originalKept` "false". A platform admin gets `guestPhone` empty.

post.description:
For the tablet and the console, waiter or above at the booking's branch, **until 05:00 the morning after the booking's service day**, branch time - a booking starting before 05:00 belongs to the evening before, so a 01:00 booking's window closes at 05:00 that same morning. Already withdrawn: `200` with the booking as it stands. **Online only** - not for the offline queue.

post.summary: Mark a booking as a no-show, and free the table
post.description:
The same action as `release` with `outcome: 1`, under the name the tablet's late-booking panel uses - one implementation, two doors, so the two cannot drift.

**Never automatic.** Prompt 2's rule that the decision belongs to a waiter applies here more than anywhere: only a person standing in the room knows whether the party is late or absent.

Counts toward the diner's rolling no-show threshold. If they telephoned to say they could not come, use `release` with `outcome: 2` instead - a diner who let the venue know must not be punished for it.

**Only from the booking's start.** Before `startUtc` nobody can have failed to come, so the answer is `409 reservation-not-started` (`context.reservationId`, `context.startUtc`) and nothing changes - the hold stays, the booking stays confirmed. From the start itself there is no further wait: the branch's grace period times the late nudge, and whether a party past their time is late or absent is the waiter's call. To let a booking go earlier, use `release` with `outcome: 2`.

**The guest is told** every time (push `reservation.no-show`, feed `booking-no-show`), and who marked it is recorded. It counts toward a **no-show block** (three in three days, see `docs/reservations.md`) only when marked after the start plus the branch's grace (or the extended hold), and at most one per venue per service day counts. Marked by mistake? `POST /api/reservations/{id}/undo-no-show` until 05:00 the next morning. When this no-show blocked the guest, the answer's `guestBlockedUntilUtc` says until when.

post.description:
**Two outcomes, and the difference matters to the diner.**

| `outcome` | Booking becomes | Counts toward the no-show threshold |
|---|---|---|
| `1` NoShow | `NoShow` | **Yes** |
| `2` CancelledByVenue | `CancelledByVenue` | **No** |

Render these as two buttons - *release, marked no-show* and *release, they let us know*. With one button a busy waiter taps it for both, and the threshold ends up punishing the people who phoned ahead. A table out of service is always the second one: a broken chair is the venue's doing.

The table is freed when it is **held for this booking**, through the state machine, so the audit row is written and the branch change sequence moves. A table somebody is **sitting at** is left alone - the booking is released either way, and a floor plan that shows an occupied table as free costs more than a stale hold.

**`outcome: 1` only from the booking's start.** Before `startUtc` a no-show is refused with `409 reservation-not-started` (`context.reservationId`, `context.startUtc`) and nothing changes. `outcome: 2` is allowed at any time, and so is the table's own `release-hold`.

What the staff tablet's *awaiting approval* panel polls (every ten seconds or so) before calling `approve` or `reject`. Each item: `reservation` (the `ReservationView` - code, start, party, table, room, guest name, and `guestPhone` for calling), `approvalExpiresAtUtc` (count down to it - fifteen minutes at short notice, two hours for a booking waiting on the guest before it, whom the floor calls; null for a booking that waits as long as it takes), `trigger` (the `ApprovalTrigger`, 4 ShortNotice), and the table's context that day: `previousBooking` (`reservationId`, `startUtc`, `localStartTime`, `partySize`, `guestName`, `guestPhone`, `status` - the booking before it, cancelled ones skipped), `nextBooking` (`reservationId`, `startUtc`, `localStartTime`, `partySize`) and `currentSitting` (`seatedAtUtc`, `partySize` - absent when a diner's scan opened the table and only guessed). Each is absent when there is none, like every null in this API.

One query however many are waiting. A waiter or above at this branch; an owner or general manager at any branch of their venue. A platform admin reads the list with every guest number blank (`guestPhone` empty, `previousBooking.guestPhone` absent).

post.summary: Key in an order spoken at the table
post.description:
The same code path as a diner's order, deliberately: the total is only right if **every** order goes through the system.

**Straight to the kitchen.** A waiter's order is answered with `status` `InKitchen`: the waiter who took it at the table is the check a phone's order waits at `New` for, so there is no second send. The tab's stream carries `OrderPlaced` and then `OrderStatusChanged` (New -> InKitchen) in the same commit.

**On a tab waiting for admission too** - staff may always order - and it **never admits the tab**: the phones on it still wait for a waiter's Admit (`POST /api/tabs/{tabId}/admit`).

`onBehalfOfParticipantId` is what keeps "everyone pays their own" working. Without it the line is **attributed to the table** and splits across everyone present - a real answer rather than a wrong one, and one whose cost the venue can see in its own numbers.

**Who, per line.** `items[i].participantId` names the guest one line is for and overrides `onBehalfOfParticipantId` for that line alone, so a round with the table's latte, Narine's steak and Aram's coffee is **one order and one kitchen ticket**, each dish on the person who ate it. Every line in the response carries `onBehalfOfParticipantId`: its own guest, else the order's, and absent on a shared line. `onBehalfOfParticipantId` on the order is a default for the lines that name nobody, not a claim on the order. Both fields are checked by one rule - an approved participant on this tab.

**A shared line has no owner.** `isShared` splits the line across everyone present whatever `onBehalfOfParticipantId` says, as it always did; a line that is `isShared` **and** names a `participantId` contradicts itself and is refused. Every refusal refuses the whole send.

When `onBehalfOfParticipantId` or a line's `participantId` is not on this tab - made up, or a guest at another table - `context` names it: `field` (`onBehalfOfParticipantId` or `items[i].participantId`) and `participantId`. Any other 404 here (a dish on no menu, an unknown tab) has no `context`.

409.description: `tab-not-accepting-orders`: the tab takes no more orders. `context.status` says why - 2 Closing (the bill has been asked for), 3 Closed (paid and settled), 4 Abandoned (written off). Also `menu-item-unavailable`, with the dish named, and `conflicting-state`: with `context.participantId` when a guest the order named is not orderable for (not let on yet, or taken off), without it for anything else.

Refused once the tab has been paid against: that is a refund, which is a different thing with its own rail.

post.description:
Exactly one of `percent` and `amountAmd`. A `tabOrderLineId` applies it to that line; leaving it out applies it to the whole tab.

**The service charge is computed after this**, so comping a dish comps its service charge with it - which is what a manager means by comping a dish.

Visible to the diner with its reason, for the same reason a void is.

`reductionAmd` is what this adjustment itself took off, in the bill's order - the amount the History and the reports give it - not the subtotal's drop: a comp under a standing tab-wide discount takes its line's whole price, while the subtotal drops by less.

post.summary: Take cash at the table
post.description:
The amount is **reserved against the remaining balance under the tab's row version** before anything is recorded, then marked succeeded in the same call. The two-step shape exists so a wallet provider can sit in `Reserved` while it is being called.

Paying more than is owed is refused **with the current balance in the body** - the waiter is standing at the table and needs the number, and the usual cause is somebody settling in the app while the waiter was typing.

Partial payments are normal and expected. When the balance reaches zero the tab closes and its sitting closes with it - but **the table is not freed**. That stays an explicit waiter action, because a party that has paid usually sits on for another twenty minutes.

`tipAmd` is recorded and kept **entirely outside** `paidAmd` and `remainingAmd`.

**This is not a fiscal receipt.** The venue's registered cash register still issues one.

reason.description: Why, as somebody typed it.

booking's decision from its request.

lines and who added and voided each. Exactly one header is present for those three subjects; any other subject has
its entries and no header.

Yalla.Application.Activity.BookingTimeli.description: A booking's header on its timeline.

Yalla.Application.Activity.DailySales.description: A day's sales on a person's chart.

kpis.description: Their row, as on Staff → Results.

dailySales.description: As on a person's page: one entry per local date, a week ending on `to` at least.

recent.description: Every list's first page, `limit` entries each.

My results in one read: the caller's numbers, their chart and the first page of every recent list - what the
staff phone's screen shows for a period, which took one `/api/staff/me/performance` call per list before.

kpis.description: Their row, as on Staff → Results.

dailySales.description: One entry per local date from six days before `to` (or `from`, when earlier) to `to`, zero days included.

Yalla.Application.Activity.PersonPerform.description: One person's page: their numbers, a day-by-day chart, and their recent work.

orders.description: Orders sent, pre-orders sent, voids, discounts, comps, bills closed in cash.

cash.description: Cash at tables and at the takeaway counter.

Yalla.Application.Activity.RecentLists.description:
The first page of each of a person's recent lists, read together for My results. Each page is the one
`/api/staff/me/performance?list=…` answers, cursor included, so "more" continues there.

items.description: This page - History entries, with `seconds` where the action measures it.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor`; absent on the last page.

Yalla.Application.Activity.RecentPage.description: A page of one of a person's recent lists, newest first.

staff.description: One row per person with anything in the window, and every active waiter and manager of the branch.

Yalla.Application.Activity.StaffPerforma.description: Staff → Results: everybody's numbers over the window, and the branch's.

role.description: What a staff member is allowed to do, coarsely. Authorisation itself is a later task.

tables.description: Closed bills in the window with a share of their sale theirs, or that were theirs at the close.

salesAmd.description: Their share of those bills' totals, service charge included - whole dram, in the proportion of the lines ordered while the table was theirs.

averageCheckAmd.description: Sales over tables, rounded; 0 with no tables.

tipsAmd.description: Tips on payments taken while the table was theirs.

callsClaimed.description: Calls and bill requests they claimed ("I'm on it").

callClaimMedianSeconds.description: The median seconds from the call to their claim; absent with none.

messageReplyMedianSeconds.description: The median seconds from the guest's text to their reply; absent with none.

cashAmd.description: Cash they took: on bills that closed in the window, and at the takeaway counter.

cashPayments.description: How many cash payments that was.

adjustmentsAmd.description: What those took off, as the bills charged it.

Yalla.Application.Activity.StaffPerforma.description:
One person's numbers over a window. Sales, guests, tables and tips are the table's waiter's: a sale is theirs from
the order placed while the table was theirs, so a transfer moves what comes after and leaves what came before. See
`docs/activity.md`.

unattributedSalesAmd.description: The part of that no waiter held: a table nobody on staff served.

takeawayAmd.description: Takeaway collected - the revenue report's `takeawayAmd`; nobody's sale.

Yalla.Application.Activity.StaffPerforma.description:
The branch's totals over the window - counted once, not summed from the rows: a transferred table is one table, and a
median of everyone is not the sum of medians. The money matches the revenue report for the same dates.

seatedAtUtc.description: When the party sat - before the tab, often.

closedAtUtc.description: When it closed; absent while open.

status.description: 1 Open, 2 Closing, 3 Closed, 4 Abandoned.

totalAmd.description: What the bill came to - the reports' figure for it.

tipsAmd.description: Tips on its payments, outside the bill.

servers.description: The table's waiters in turn: who took it from when - the first from the seat, each transfer after.

Yalla.Application.Activity.TabTimelineHe.description: A bill's header on its timeline.

previousServerStaffMemberId.description: Whose it was; absent when nobody served it.

transferredAtUtc.description: From when - what came before stays with the earlier waiter.

tableSessionId.description: The sitting, which carries the waiter.

wasReplay.description: Already theirs: answered as done, nothing written.

Yalla.Application.Activity.TakeawayTimel.description: A takeaway order's header on its timeline.

lineTotalAmd.description: Quantity times price - zero once voided.

addedByStaffMemberId.description: The waiter who keyed it; absent for a guest's phone.

addedByName.description: That waiter's name, or the guest's display name.

addedByGuest.description: A guest ordered it from their phone.

serverStaffMemberId.description: The table's waiter when it was ordered - whose sale it is.

Yalla.Application.Activity.TimelineLine.description: A line on a bill with who did what to it.

Yalla.Application.Activity.TimelineServe.description: A waiter's turn at a table.

onShiftNow.description: A shift of theirs at this branch runs now.

openTables.description: The tables they serve at this branch now - live sittings whose waiter they are.

Yalla.Application.Activity.TransferTarge.description: One person who may take the table. Nothing more personal than a name and a role.

items.description: On shift first, then by name.

Yalla.Application.Activity.TransferTarge.description: Who the table can be handed to - the transfer sheet's list, for a phone that lists nobody else.

id.description: Their staff member id - what `POST /api/auth/staff/pin` takes on this phone.

role.description: What a staff member is allowed to do, coarsely. Authorisation itself is a later task.

Yalla.Application.Auth.BoundStaffMemberV.description: The person a phone belongs to.

code.description: The code. Shown once, never retrievable again - only its hash is stored.

branchId.description: The branch the resulting device will be bound to.

Yalla.Application.Auth.DeviceEnrolmentCo.description: A one-time code a manager reads out to a tablet being enrolled.

deviceToken.description: Long-lived bearer token identifying the tablet. It can do exactly one thing: offer a PIN.

deviceId.description: The enrolled device, revocable from the admin panel.

branchId.description: The one branch this tablet is bound to.

deviceName.description: The name the manager gave it.

expiresAtUtc.description: When the device token itself expires and the tablet must re-enrol.

Yalla.Application.Auth.DeviceEnrolmentRe.description: What a tablet gets back for a redeemed enrolment code.

accessToken.description: Bearer token for the diner surface. Short-lived.

refreshToken.description: Rotating handle. Send it once; the response carries its successor.

dinerUserId.description: The account, created on first successful verification.

isNewAccount.description: True when this verification created the account.

Yalla.Application.Auth.DinerSignInResult.description: Tokens issued to a diner who verified their phone number.

clientDeviceId.description: The identifier the client minted for itself.

branchId.description: The one branch it can act on.

branchName.description: That branch, in words, because an id on a counter screen means nothing.

venueName.description: The venue, for a chain where two branches share a name.

features.description:
The features the platform allows at the branch, in numeric order, for the PIN screen and the app shell before
anybody signs in (a kitchen screen without kitchen display 9, a phone without staff phone 8). Absent only from a
response built before 2026-10-27.

kind.description: What an enrolled `StaffDevice` is. Stored as the integer; never renumber.

boundStaffMember.description: On a phone, the one person whose PIN opens it; absent on a tablet.

Yalla.Application.Auth.EnrolledDeviceVie.description: Where an enrolled device thinks it is, shown on the PIN screen before anybody taps.

code.description:
Ten characters, shown as `XXXXX-XXXXX`. Returned once; only its hash is stored. Case and the dash do not
matter when typed.

expiresAtUtc.description: Ten minutes from now. A newer code for the same person replaces this one.

pairingUrl.description: What the QR carries: the staff app's pairing page with the code in the fragment.

branchId.description: The branch the phone will be bound to.

Yalla.Application.Auth.PhonePairingCodeR.description: A code that pairs one person's phone to them, as the console shows it in a QR.

role.description: What a staff member is allowed to do, coarsely. Authorisation itself is a later task.

branchId.description: The branch the phone will be bound to.

Yalla.Application.Auth.PhonePairingPrevi.description: Who a pairing code is for, so the phone can ask "is this you?" before the PIN.

device.description: Exactly what `POST /api/auth/staff/enrol` answers - keep the device token.

session.description: Exactly what `POST /api/auth/staff/pin` answers - the person is signed in.

Yalla.Application.Auth.PhonePairingResul.description: A paired phone: its device token and a session for its person, as enrolment and a PIN would give.

sms.description:
A one-time code by SMS can be sent: a provider is configured, or this is Development, where the
code goes to the log. False means `request-code` answers `sms-unavailable`.

telegram.description: The Telegram bot is on, so `/api/auth/diner/telegram` is mapped.

Yalla.Application.Auth.PhoneProofChannel.description: Which ways of proving a phone number this deployment offers.

refreshToken.description: The successor handle. The one you sent is now dead.

Yalla.Application.Auth.RefreshResult.description: A refreshed access token and the refresh token that replaces the one just spent.

endedSessions.description: How many other sign-ins could still carry on and now cannot. Zero is an answer.

Yalla.Application.Auth.SignedOutElsewher.description: What signing the other sign-ins out ended.

branchId.description: The branch it is bound to.

enrolledAtUtc.description: When it redeemed its enrolment code.

lastSeenAtUtc.description: Last time a token from it was used. Null if never.

isRevoked.description: True once a manager killed it. Revocation is permanent; re-enrol instead.

kind.description: What an enrolled `StaffDevice` is. Stored as the integer; never renumber.

boundStaffMember.description: A phone's person; absent on a tablet.

revokedAtUtc.description: When it was revoked or unpaired; absent while live.

platform.description:
A phone's platform as it said when it paired (`1` other ... `7` Linux); absent on a tablet and on a phone
paired before 2026-10-26.

browser.description: A phone's browser as it said when it paired; absent on a tablet, or when it did not say.

Yalla.Application.Auth.StaffDeviceSummar.description: One enrolled tablet, as the admin panel lists it.

role.description: What a staff member is allowed to do, coarsely. Authorisation itself is a later task.

onShiftNow.description: A shift at this branch runs now: StartsAtUtc at or before now, EndsAtUtc after it.

startsAt.description: The shift's start, branch wall clock; absent with no shift to report.

endsAt.description: Its end, branch wall clock, on the next date when EndsNextDay; absent with no shift.

endsNextDay.description: The shift ends after midnight - including at exactly 00:00. False with no shift.

startsAtUtc.description:
The start as an instant, so a screen left open can tell when it begins; absent with no shift. A start in an hour
the clocks skip is read on the clock from before the change: 02:30 that night is 03:30 summer time.

endsAtUtc.description: The end as an instant, so a screen left open can tell when it is over; absent with no shift.

Yalla.Application.Auth.StaffRosterEntry.description:
One person who may tap a PIN on this tablet, as its PIN screen lists them - and whether they are on
shift, so the screen can put those people first.

accessToken.description: Bearer token carrying the staff member, their role and their branch.

renewalToken.description:
Handle the tablet exchanges to stay signed in. Rotates on every use, and stops working after
thirty minutes of inactivity - at which point the PIN is needed again.

staffMemberId.description: Who is acting. This is the id that lands in the audit log.

fullName.description: Shown on the tablet so the waiter can see whose session is open.

role.description: What a staff member is allowed to do, coarsely. Authorisation itself is a later task.

branchId.description: The branch this session may act on, and only this one.

features.description:
The features the platform allows at the branch, in numeric order - read again on every renewal, so a change reaches
the tablet within one. Hide what is not listed (table service 5, takeaway 4, guest messages 6, kitchen display 9,
staff phone 8, pre-orders 3); the venue's own switches still apply inside it.

Yalla.Application.Auth.StaffSessionResul.description: A staff member's session on a tablet, opened by a PIN.

accessToken.description: Bearer token valid only for TabId.

expiresAtUtc.description: When it stops working - the tab's close, plus a receipt grace period.

participantId.description: This person's row on the tab.

tabId.description: The one tab this token can touch.

branchId.description: The branch the tab is in.

displayName.description: What the host sees. Changeable, and not an account.

canOrder.description: Whether this participant may add items.

Yalla.Application.Auth.TabParticipantTok.description: The tab-scoped token handed to someone who scanned a QR code or redeemed a join token.

state.description:
`pending` while the bot has not been handed the number; `verified` exactly once,
            with SignIn set. After that the challenge is spent and answers 410.

signIn.description: The tokens, when State is `verified`. Null otherwise.

phoneE164.description:
The number Telegram handed over, in E.164, when State is `verified` -
so the app can show it without a second round trip to the profile. Null otherwise.

challengeId.description: Poll with this. Opaque, and useless to anyone who did not also open the link.

deepLinkUrl.description: `https://t.me/{bot}?start={nonce}`. Open it; Telegram starts the bot with the nonce.

expiresInSeconds.description: How long the link, and the challenge, stay usable.

pollAfterMs.description: How long to wait between claims. Polling faster than this spends the claim rate limit for nothing.

Yalla.Application.Auth.TelegramVerificat.description: What the app needs to open the bot and to poll.

staffMemberId.description: Their staff row - the one the staff routes, such as the PIN reset, address them by.

fullName.description: The name the console and the activity feed show. Theirs to change.

email.description:
The sign-in address. Not theirs to change: whoever outranks them gives them a new sign-in link for a
new address (`issueStaffSignIn`), and an owner's is changed by the platform.

role.description: What a staff member is allowed to do, coarsely. Authorisation itself is a later task.

branchId.description:
A branch manager's home branch. Absent on the wire (null) for an owner or general manager, who run every
branch - an owner's row may name a branch, and it is still not answered here.

Yalla.Application.Auth.VenueUserProfile.description: The signed-in owner's, general manager's or branch manager's own account.

lastActiveAtUtc.description: When it last renewed its token; the sign-in itself until it first does.

isCurrent.description: The sign-in the request's own token belongs to.

Yalla.Application.Auth.VenueUserSession.description:
One admin-panel sign-in that can still carry on: a refresh chain with a token that is neither
revoked, rotated nor expired.

Yalla.Application.Auth.VenueUserSessions.description: Where the venue user is signed in: the current sign-in first, then the most recently active.

accessToken.description: Bearer token for the admin surface.

role.description: What a staff member is allowed to do, coarsely. Authorisation itself is a later task.

venueId.description: The venue this account administers. Null for a platform admin, who administers all of them.

Yalla.Application.Auth.VenueUserSignInRe.description: An owner or manager signed in to the admin panel.

expiresInSeconds.description: How long the code stays usable.

maxAttempts.description: How many wrong guesses the code tolerates before it dies.

developmentCode.description: The code itself, returned only in Development so the flow can be exercised with no SMS provider wired up. Always null in any other environment.

Yalla.Application.Auth.VerificationCodeR.description: What `request-code` answers, whether or not the number has an account.

cuisine.description: Up to 120 characters. Null or blank clears it.

about.description: Up to 2000 characters. Null or blank clears it.

websiteUrl.description: An absolute http(s) URL, or null to clear.

amenities.description:
Keys from `outdoorSeating`, `wifi`, `parking`, `cardPayment`, `vegan`.
Null or empty clears them.

galleryPhotoIds.description: Photos uploaded for this branch, in display order, at most 12. Null leaves the gallery as it is; an empty list clears it.

address.description: A new street address; only applied together with coordinates.

latitude.description: Sent with Longitude to move the pin, or neither.

district.description:
The part of town, e.g. "Kentron" - printed after the venue type and cuisine, and matched by search.
Up to 60 characters, trimmed. Null or blank clears it. A listing field like the cuisine line: a
manager may set it, unlike the address, because naming the neighbourhood moves nobody's pin.

gallery.description: Pictures beyond the cover, in order.

district.description: The part of town, e.g. "Kentron", or absent.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.BranchL.description: What a branch says about itself on the diner app's browse screens.

isReadyForDiners.description:
Every line below satisfied. This is exactly what going Paid requires on the menu side, plus the
rest of the checklist - the tier switch itself only enforces the menu, because a venue may want
its tabs enabled before it has finished enrolling tablets.

floorPlanDrawn.description: At least one active table exists at the branch.

tableCount.description: How many active tables there are.

tablesLabelled.description:
Every active table carries a label. Labels are required by the entity and unique per branch, so
this is satisfied whenever there are tables at all - it is reported because the checklist has a
line for it and a silently-absent line reads as a failure.

menuCategoriesPresent.description: The branch has at least one menu category.

menuItemCount.description: How many items there are, complete or not.

incompleteMenuItemCount.description: How many items are missing a photo, a description, ingredients, allergens, a portion size or a prep time. The number that blocks going live, and the number the refusal quotes.

incompleteMenuItemIds.description: Which ones, so the console can link straight to them.

menuComplete.description: No categories missing, and no incomplete items.

openingHoursSet.description: At least one opening block exists for the week.

openingHoursDayCount.description: How many days of the week have any opening block.

reservationPolicyReviewed.description:
Somebody has saved the reservation policy at least once. A branch ships with defaults, so
"has a policy" is always true and answers nothing; this asks whether a human has looked.

staffEnrolled.description: At least one active staff member works at this branch.

deviceEnrolled.description: At least one tablet is enrolled and not revoked.

acceptsWebBookings.description: Whether the branch takes bookings from its public page. Reported, and deliberately not a blocker. A venue that does not want bookings from strangers on the internet is not an unfinished venue - most will start this way, and its public page showing the room, the menu and the hours is a perfectly good page. It is on the checklist so that leaving it off is something somebody saw and chose, rather than a default they never knew they had inherited; a line that blocked going live would instead teach every onboarder to switch it on without reading it, which is the opposite of the point.

blockers.description:
One sentence per unsatisfied line, in checklist order. The console renders its own labels; this
is for the places that need to say what is wrong without reimplementing the list - a log line,
a support answer, an email to the venue.

issues.description:
The same unsatisfied lines as Blockers, one for one and in the same order, as
stable codes a client can switch on - Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.ReadinessIssueCodes - with the count behind
the ones that have one. The platform console's venue list and Home show the first of these.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.BranchR.description: What a branch still needs before it can take diners.

id.description: The existing room this entry edits, or null for one matched by name or created.

name.description: Unique within the branch, and required.

photoIds.description: The room's photos, in the order a diner swipes them - the whole list, replacing what was there. At most Yalla.Domain.Venues.FloorAreaPhoto.MaxPhotos, each a photo uploaded for this branch (another branch's is not found here, the gallery's answer), and each in at most one room. Null or absent means none. A photo dropped from every room takes the tables pinned on it off the photo.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.FloorAr.description: A room as the editor sends it. `Id` matches an existing room; null means new.

photos.description: The room's photos, in order. Empty for a room nobody has photographed yet.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.FloorAr.description: A room as the editor reads it, with its photos in the order a diner swipes them.

warnings.description:
Things worth fixing that are not errors - today, a bookable table with no pin, which diners are
not offered.

deactivatedTables.description:
Labels of tables this save took out of service: active before, left out, kept inactive because
they have history. Not the tables already inactive - the editor leaves those out of every save,
and reporting them each time would announce a change nobody made.

removedTables.description: Labels of omitted tables deleted outright.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.FloorPl.description:
The plan as applied, plus what the editor should know: warnings that did not stop it, and which
omitted tables were deactivated rather than deleted because they have history.

areas.description: The rooms, lowest `displayOrder` first, each with its photos.

version.description:
The plan's revision, opaque. Send it back as `expectedVersion` on the replace; a save against
an older revision is refused with `floor-plan-changed`.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.FloorPl.description: The rooms, their photos, and every table with its pin.

id.description: The existing table this entry edits, or null for one matched by label or created.

label.description: What is printed on the table. Unique within the branch, and required.

floorAreaName.description: Names a room in the same plan, by name. Null for no room.

isBookable.description: False for tables that only ever take walk-ins, e.g. bar stools.

photoId.description: The photo the table is pinned on - one of its own room's`photoIds` in this plan - or null for no pin. Sent with PhotoX and PhotoY, or all three null. A diner is only offered a bookable table that has a pin.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.FloorTa.description:
A table as the editor sends it. `Id` matches an existing table; null means new - unless a
table with that label already exists in the branch, in which case it is that table, so its QR
code survives an editor that lost the id.

isBookable.description: False for tables that only ever take walk-ins.

isActive.description: False for a table deactivated because it has history.

qrToken.description: The token behind the QR code on the table.

status.description: The physical state of a table: what somebody did to it.

isDeletable.description: Whether a delete would remove it rather than deactivate it.

photoId.description: The room photo it is pinned on, or null. Always one of its own room's photos.

photoX.description: Where the pin sits on that photo, 0 (left) to 1 (right); null with no pin.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.FloorTa.description: A table as the editor reads it.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Opening.description: One opening block as the client sends it. `closesNextDay` is derived, not sent.

closesAt.description: Wall clock; on the next date when ClosesNextDay.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Opening.description: One block of a special day.
One opening block as the client supplies it. `ClosesNextDay` is derived, not sent.

phoneE164.description:
E.164, e.g. `+37411223344`. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped before validation.
Null or blank clears the number.

acceptsWebBookings.description: Whether to offer booking on the public page.

coverPhotoId.description: A photo uploaded for this branch, or null to clear the picture. One uploaded for another branch is not found here, the same answer a menu item gets for a foreign photo.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.PublicP.description: The same settings, as written. All are replaced at once.

phoneE164.description: The published contact number in E.164, or null when there is none.

acceptsWebBookings.description:
Whether the public page offers booking. See
Yalla.Domain.Venues.Branch.AcceptsWebBookings for why this is false until somebody
says otherwise.

coverPhoto.description:
The venue card's picture - the first thing a stranger sees on the public page and in the diner
app's list - or null when there is none yet.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.PublicP.description: The two settings that decide what a branch publishes to anybody with its link.

code.description: One of Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.ReadinessIssueCodes.

count.description:
How many, when the line counts something - the unfinished dishes for
`incomplete-dishes`. Absent for a line that is simply missing.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Readine.description: One thing a branch still lacks, as a code and, where it has one, the count behind it.

areas.description: Every room in the plan, each with its photos.

tables.description: Every table in the plan, each with its pin or none.

expectedVersion.description: Required. The `version` the editor loaded. A plan changed since then is refused with `409 floor-plan-changed` and `context.currentVersion`, and nothing is written.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Replace.description: The whole plan - rooms, their photos and every table's pin - replaced in one atomic call.

days.description: Every special day from today at the branch on - `[]` clears them. An entry dated before today is history and is ignored, not refused: a console left open past midnight still saves the rest.

expectedVersion.description: Required. The `version` the editor loaded. A list saved since then is refused with `409 concurrent-update` and `context.currentVersion`, and nothing is written.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Replace.description: The console's save of the special days: the whole list from today on, against the revision it loaded.

max.description: The most a save accepts, or null where there is no ceiling.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Reserva.description: One field's editing bounds, as Yalla.Domain.Venues.ReservationPolicyLimits enforces them.

policy.description: The policy now in force, as stored.

affectedExistingReservations.description: How many live bookings now fall outside the new rules - beyond the shortened window, or booked under a longer turn time. They were not changed: a settings edit never rewrites or cancels a booking. The new rules apply to future bookings only.

affectedReservationIds.description: Which ones, so the panel can show them.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Reserva.description: The policy after the change, and what the change did not do.
Every field of the policy, as written. The whole form is replaced at once.

defaults.description: The policy a branch of this venue's type starts with.

bounds.description: Every bounded field, in the order the form lists them.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Reserva.description:
What a branch's policy ships with and the bounds a save is held to - read from the server so the
console's "default" line and its reset cannot drift from M:Yalla.Domain.Venues.ReservationPolicy.DefaultFor(Yalla.Domain.Enums.VenueType).
Every field of the owned Yalla.Domain.Venues.ReservationPolicy, as read.

date.description: The branch's local date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. At most a year and a day out; an entry before today at the branch is history and is ignored.

note.description: What a diner is told - "New Year". Optional; trimmed, blank is none, at most 60 characters.

blocks.description: The opening blocks that open on the date. Empty is closed all day. At most four; they may touch but not overlap. A closing time at or before the opening time means after midnight, as in the weekly hours.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Special.description: One special day as the console sends it.

note.description: What a diner is told; absent when there is none.

closed.description: Closed all day: Blocks is empty.

blocks.description: The blocks that open on the date, earliest first. They replace the weekday's hours.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Special.description: One special day as every read returns it - the console's list, the public pages, the day's slots.

version.description: The list's revision now; the next save sends it as `expectedVersion`.

days.description: The special days as saved, from the service date on as Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.SpecialOpeningDaysView.Days.

affectedExistingReservations.description: How many live future bookings - confirmed, or waiting for approval - this save put outside the hours: on a date whose special day was added, removed or given other blocks, or just after midnight following one, that fitted the hours before the save and do not now. They were not changed or cancelled: a settings edit never touches a booking. Somebody has to call those guests.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Special.description: What saving the special days did.

version.description:
The list's revision. Opaque: send it back as `expectedVersion` with the next save, which is refused with
`409 concurrent-update` if somebody saved in between.

days.description:
The special days from the branch's service date on, earliest first: today's on - and, while last night's special block
is still running past midnight, yesterday's first. That one is read-only: a save replaces today on, so it is kept.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.Special.description: The branch's special days as the console edits them, with the revision it is editing.

deleted.description: Removed outright: it had never been used.

deactivated.description: Kept and switched off: it has reservations, seatings or tabs.

message.description: Which of the two happened, for the manager.

floorPlanVersion.description:
The plan's version after the delete. Either outcome changes the plan and moves it, so an editor
that loaded the plan before is refused rather than saving the table back; the editor that made
the delete adopts this to keep its own draft current.

Yalla.Application.BranchSettings.TableDe.description: What deleting a table did: removed outright, or deactivated because it has history.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerFavoriteLi.description: The diner's favourites, newest first. A place that is not published is left out.

listing.description: The card, exactly as the public list serves it - with `distanceKm` when `lat`/`lng` were sent.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerFavoriteVi.description: One of the diner's favourite places (K11).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; absent on the last page.

unreadCount.description: Unread entries across the whole feed, not only this page - the badge.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerNotificati.description: A page of the feed, newest first.

notificationId.description: The entry; what `upTo` and `ids` name when marking read.

kind.description:
`booking-reminder`, `booking-confirmed`, `booking-declined`,
            `booking-cancelled-by-venue`, `order-ready`, `review-hidden`, `review-replied`,
            `table-request`, `table-request-decided`, `booking-changed-by-link`,
            `booking-cancelled-by-link`, `bookings-blocked-no-shows`, `booking-no-show`,
            `bookings-unblocked` or `booking-on-your-way`. The app writes the text.

params.description:
String values the app's text is built from, as they were when the entry was written: for bookings
`venueName`, `branchName`, `date` (yyyy-MM-dd), `time` (HH:mm), `partySize`,
`reservationCode`; for an order `venueName`, `branchName`, `tableLabel`; for a
review `venueName`, `branchName`, `reviewId`.

branchId.description: The place, when there is one.

branchName.description: The place's name now, or as written when the branch is gone.

reservationId.description: The booking, for the booking kinds.

createdAtUtc.description: When it appeared - for a reminder, when the reminder was due.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerNotificati.description: One entry in the diner's notifications feed (K12).

name.description: The item name as it read when ordered.

unitPriceAmd.description: Whole dram per unit, as it stood when ordered.

lineTotalAmd.description: Quantity × unit price, or 0 once voided.

note.description: The kitchen note, or absent.

isVoided.description: Removed by staff. Kept on the order, at zero, rather than vanishing.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerOrderItem.description: One line on a diner's order.

status.description: An app status - see Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerOrderStatuses.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerOrderTimel.description: When the order reached a status.

tabId.description: The tab it was placed against. Absent on a takeaway order, which has no tab.

kind.description: `"dineIn"` for an order on a table's tab, `"takeaway"` for a takeaway order.

status.description: App status - see Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerOrderStatuses.

kitchenStatus.description: Kitchen-facing progress of one order placed against a tab.

tableLabel.description: The table's label. Empty on a takeaway order.

partySize.description: The seated party's size. 0 on a takeaway order.

placedAtUtc.description: When it was sent to the kitchen.

totalAmd.description: Sum of the non-voided lines, whole dram, before service charge.

timeline.description: Oldest first; the last entry is the current status.

canCancel.description:
False on a dine-in order: voiding it is a staff action on the kitchen rail. True on a takeaway order while the venue
has not answered it - `POST /api/diner/takeaway-orders/{id}/cancel`.

takeaway.description: The takeaway order's own facts - code, exact status, pickup and ready times. Absent on dine-in.

messages.description:
A takeaway order's thread with the venue in one line - unread, the last message, whether it takes messages. Absent on
dine-in, and on an order with no thread that takes none. See `docs/messages.md`.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerOrderView.description: One order the diner is on, receipt-shaped, for the Orders tab.

username.description: Sign-in name, lowercased. Null for an account the code flow created and nobody has filled in.

email.description: Sign-in address, lowercased. Null until given.

phoneVerified.description: Whether a one-time code to that number has ever been passed.

displayName.description: What the venue calls this person.

hasPassword.description: Whether a password sign-in exists. False for a code-only account.

photo.description: The profile picture's three links, or null when there is none.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerProfileVie.description: A diner's own account, as their app shows it on the profile screen.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the rating or text last changed. Re-sending the same review does not move it.

publicAuthorName.description: The name the public list shows it under - see `BranchReview.PublicAuthorName`.

hidden.description: Taken down by moderation: the diner still sees it here, nobody else sees it anywhere.

reply.description:
The venue's public reply, or null, signed as the public reads it ("Aram H."). The author sees it here
even while the review is hidden.

Yalla.Application.Diners.DinerReviewView.description: The signed-in diner's own review of one branch.

status.description: Where a takeaway order stands. Stored as an int, so every number is pinned (`PersistedEnumValueTests`).

pickupAsap.description: Ordered for as soon as possible.

requestedPickupUtc.description: When the guest asked for it.

readyAtUtc.description: When the venue promised it. Absent until accepted.

upTo.description: Marks this entry and every older one read.

ids.description: Marks these entries read; at most 200.

branchIds.description:
At most 500. Each is added when missing; nothing is ever removed. An unknown or unpublished place is
skipped rather than refused - a heart made weeks ago may be for a place that has since closed.

Yalla.Application.Diners.MergeFavoritesC.description: Body of `PUT /api/diner/favorites`: hearts made while signed out, merged into the account.

reason.description: `spam`, `offensive`, `not-a-visit`, `personal-info` or `other`.

note.description: Optional detail, at most 500 characters.

text.description: Optional, at most 1000 characters. Blank clears it.

Yalla.Application.Diners.SubmitBranchRev.description: Body of the diner's review routes.

sequence.description: Position in the stream. Strictly increasing per branch.

tableStateChangeId.description: The audit row this came from.

diningTableId.description: The table that changed. Null only on a Signal 8 entry, which is about the takeaway counter.

tableLabel.description: Its label, so a client can render without a second lookup. Null when there is no table.

fromStatus.description: The physical state of a table: what somebody did to it.

toStatus.description: The physical state of a table: what somebody did to it.

reason.description: Free text recorded with the transition.

actorId.description: Who acted. Null only for a System change.

tableSessionId.description: The seating opened or closed by this change, when there was one.

reservationId.description: The booking involved, when there was one.

tabId.description: The tab involved, when there was one - always on a Signal entry.

signal.description:
Set when the entry is about more than the table's status: 1 a scan's tab is waiting to be let in, 2 it was
admitted, 3 it was turned away (on the Occupied-to-Free row when that freed the table) - refetch the
awaiting-admission list; 4 a booking the platform cancelled for a no-show block and 5 any other booking event -
re-read the floor; 6 a booking's pre-order changed - re-read the pre-order rail; 7 the table was handed to another
waiter - re-read the floor; 8 a takeaway order was placed, accepted, declined, cancelled, marked ready, collected or
marked not collected - re-read the takeaway counter and the kitchen's queue (no table, both statuses Free). Absent on
every ordinary change. A same-status row (4 to 8) is never folded.

Yalla.Application.Floor.BranchChange.description: One entry in a branch's change stream, as a client catching up reads it.

afterSequence.description: The sequence the caller asked to start after.

maxSequence.description: The branch's highest sequence right now. Zero when nothing has happened.

hasMore.description: True when the page hit its cap and there are further entries before MaxSequence.

Yalla.Application.Floor.BranchChangePage.description: A page of a branch's change stream, and where the stream currently ends.

timeZoneId.description: IANA zone, so a client can render Yalla.Application.Floor.TableFloorState.NextReservationStartUtc locally.

asOfUtc.description:
The instant the derived states were computed for. Every `ReservedSoon` in this
payload is relative to this, not to the client's clock.

maxSequence.description: The branch's highest change-log sequence at the moment this was read.

messages.description:
The branch's guest messages at a glance - the Messages tab's badge and the remind - so the tablet needs no second
read to badge. See `docs/messages.md`.

Yalla.Application.Floor.BranchFloorState.description:
Every active table in one branch with its live state, as of one instant: what the staff floor
screen lists, grouped by room.

unreadTotal.description:
Guest messages nobody at the venue has read - typed ones and answers - in threads that are open or had a message in
the last 24 hours: the same threads as the Messages tab.

oldestUnansweredUtc.description:
The oldest typed guest message the venue has not answered since (with a text or an ask), across those threads that
are still open: ring once it has waited the venue's `remindAfterMinutes`. A guest's answer to "are you
coming?" never waits - it is counted in UnreadTotal only. Absent when nothing waits.

Yalla.Application.Floor.FloorMessages.description: The branch's guest messages on the floor.

photoId.description:
The room photo the table is pinned on, or null when it has no pin. Staff seat an unpinned
table like any other; diners are not offered one.

photoX.description: Where the pin sits on Yalla.Application.Floor.TableFloorState.PhotoId, 0-1 across; null when there is no pin.

photoY.description: Where the pin sits on Yalla.Application.Floor.TableFloorState.PhotoId, 0-1 down; null when there is no pin.

physicalStatus.description: The physical state of a table: what somebody did to it.

state.description:
What a client should draw for a table: its physical Yalla.Domain.Enums.TableStatus with the
reservation overlay applied.

rowVersion.description: The table's row version, base64, as it stood when this floor was read.

currentSessionId.description: The open occupancy, when somebody is sitting here.

openTabId.description: The open tab on this table, when the party sitting here has one.

openTabAwaitingAdmission.description:
True when Yalla.Application.Floor.TableFloorState.OpenTabId was opened by a scan with no proved number and waits for a waiter
to admit it before anybody on it can order. The tablet's table panel offers Admit / Reject.

serverStaffMemberId.description:
The waiter whose table this is - who seated it or opened its tab, or the first to order on it, until a transfer
(`POST /api/tabs/{tabId}/transfer`). Absent with nobody seated, or nobody on staff serving yet.

serverName.description: That waiter's name as stored now.

nextReservationId.description: The next relevant booking, so the staff app can seat it straight from the floor.

freeUntilUtc.description:
How long this table can be given away for: the next booking's start less the branch's
turnaround buffer. Null when nothing is booked.

nextReservationPromisedFreeByUtc.description:
The time the next booking's guest promised to free the table by - "must free by 21:25" on the
next-booking line - or absent when they made no such promise.

nextReservationPhoneUnverified.description:
True when the next booking was made without a proved phone number - "number not verified" beside
it. False when there is no next booking.

nextReservationGuestConfirmedOnWayAtUtc.description:
When the next booking's guest answered "yes, I'm on my way" - asked of every booking 30 minutes before (45 while
a pre-order waits). Set, the waiter does not call; `null` when they have not said.

nextReservationGuestRunningLateMinutes.description: The next booking's guest said they are running late: 10, 15 or 30 minutes. `null` when they have not.

nextReservationStaffAskedOnMyWayAtUtc.description: When somebody at the venue last asked the next booking's guest "are you coming?". `null` until asked.

nextReservationGuestRecord.description:
The next booking's guest record - as on the console's list, and under the same rule: a proved account behind
it and the booking today or still to come. Absent otherwise. See Yalla.Application.Reservations.GuestRecord.

sittingGuestRecord.description:
The guest record of the party sitting here now, when they were seated against a booking a proved account
made. Absent for a walk-in, a scan, or nobody.

sittingPromisedFreeByUtc.description:
The time the party sitting here now promised to free the table by, when they were seated against
a booking that made such a promise; absent otherwise.

nextReservationUnreadMessages.description: Unread guest messages in the next booking's thread - the table tile's and the Now rail's badge. 0 without one.

sittingUnreadMessages.description: Unread guest messages in the thread of the booking the party sitting here came in on. 0 without one.

Yalla.Application.Floor.TableFloorState.description: One table's physical state plus the derived reservation overlay.

photo.description: The three links, ready to attach to a menu item or a branch.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the processed bytes, which is also part of the storage path.

wasDeduplicated.description:
True when these exact bytes were already stored for this branch and the existing photo was
returned. Reported rather than hidden - an upload that wrote nothing looks like a failure.

thumbnailUrl.description: Small square, for lists and the floor screen.

cardUrl.description: Menu card size - what a diner actually looks at.

width.description: Pixel width of the full variant. Null for a migrated photo.

height.description: Pixel height of the full variant. Null for a migrated photo.

Yalla.Application.Media.PhotoView.description: One photo as a client consumes it: three URLs and the id behind them.

branchId.description: The branch. Menus belong to branches, not venues - see `SCHEMA.md`.

categories.description: Every category in display order, each with its items.

Yalla.Application.Menus.BranchMenuView.description: One branch's whole menu, as a diner reads it.

displayOrder.description: Where it goes; absent puts it last, after every category the branch has.

spiceLevel.description: How hot a dish is, so the diner does not have to ask.

Yalla.Application.Menus.CreateMenuItemCo.description: A new item. Only a name and a price are required.

Yalla.Application.Menus.MenuItemDeletion.description: What deleting an item did: removed, or deactivated because order lines reference it.

photo.description: One photo as a client consumes it: three URLs and the id behind them.

spiceLevel.description: How hot a dish is, so the diner does not have to ask.

Yalla.Application.Menus.MenuItemView.description: One menu item as a client reads it.

categoryIds.description: Every category of the branch, each exactly once, first to last. A list that leaves one out, names one twice or names another branch's is refused whole (422 `categoryIds``conflict`) - the console is looking at a stale menu and should reload it.

Yalla.Application.Menus.ReorderMenuCateg.description: A new order for every category of a branch.

itemIds.description: Every item of the category, each exactly once, first to last; refused whole otherwise.

Yalla.Application.Menus.ReorderMenuItems.description: A new order for every item of one category.

Yalla.Application.Menus.UpdateMenuItemCo.description: Patch an item. Only supplied fields change; null means "not supplied", never "clear this".

items.description:
Threads that are open or had a message in the last 24 hours: those with a typed guest message unanswered first (the
longest waiting first), then the rest, newest first.

unreadTotal.description: Unread guest messages across Items - the tab's badge.

remindAfterMinutes.description: Ring when a typed guest message has waited this long unanswered.

templates.description: The venue's quick replies; absent for the app's default set.

waitersCanWrite.description: Whether waiters may write (managers always may).

Yalla.Application.Messages.BranchConvers.description: The branch's threads for the tablet's Messages tab.

id.description: The booking's or the order's id.

venueName.description: The venue - the only name the guest sees on the venue's side.

startUtc.description: A booking's start. Absent on a takeaway order.

localDate.description: A booking's day on the branch's wall clock, `yyyy-MM-dd`. Absent on a takeaway order.

localTime.description: A booking's start on the branch's wall clock, `HH:mm`. Absent on a takeaway order.

partySize.description: A booking's party. Absent on a takeaway order.

tableLabel.description: A booking's table. Absent on a takeaway order.

takeawayCode.description: An order's code, "T-482". Absent on a booking.

readyAtLocal.description:
An order's ready time on the branch's wall clock, `HH:mm` - the promised time once accepted, the requested one
before. Absent on a booking.

readyAtUtc.description: The same instant. Absent on a booking.

outcome.description:
The staff view only - absent on the guest's: what became of the subject. A booking: `came`, `no-show`,
`cancelled`, `declined` or `upcoming`. An order: `collected`, `no-show`, `declined`,
`cancelled` or `in-progress`.

Yalla.Application.Messages.ConversationS.description:
A thread's subject as the header shows it - "Today 19:30 · 4 guests · table 6", or "Takeaway · T-482 · ready 19:10" -
in parts, so each client writes the line in its own language.

kind.description:
`text` (has `text`), `ask-coming` (the venue's "are you coming?"), `answer` (has `answer`) or
            `status` (has `status`). Write the words for the last three in the reader's language.

text.description: The words of a `text` message - plain text, never to be linkified. Absent for the other kinds.

answer.description: An `answer`'s facts. Absent for the other kinds.

status.description: A `status` line's facts. Absent for the other kinds.

createdAtUtc.description: When it was written. "Seen" under a guest message: it is not after `venueLastReadUtc`.

Yalla.Application.Messages.DinerConversa.description: One message as the guest sees it. No staff names: the venue's side is the venue.

conversationId.description: The thread; absent while nobody has written yet (and `messages` is empty).

subject.description: What it is about - the header.

open.description:
Takes messages now: a booking until two hours after it ends (or after it was cancelled, declined, missed or
completed); an order until two hours after it was collected, declined, cancelled or not collected. Closed: no
composer - the "closed" note instead; the thread stays readable for 30 days.

closesAtUtc.description: When it closes, or closed. Absent while a takeaway order is still moving.

guestsCanWrite.description: The venue takes typed messages. False: no composer - "reply with the buttons or call".

venuePhone.description: The branch's number for the call button, E.164. Absent when it has none on file.

pendingAsk.description:
The venue asked "are you coming?", nobody has answered since, and the answer is still taken (a confirmed booking,
from two hours before its start until its end): show the answer bar.

venueLastReadUtc.description: When the venue last read the thread: a guest message not after it is "seen".

unreadCount.description: What the venue wrote since the guest last read the thread.

Yalla.Application.Messages.DinerConversa.description: A booking's or a takeaway order's thread, as its guest reads it.

conversationId.description: The thread - made by this message when it was the first.

text.description: What was stored: the text trimmed.

wasReplay.description: The same `clientCommandId` wrote it before: nothing new was written.

Yalla.Application.Messages.DinerMessageR.description: The answer to the guest's send: the message as written, and its thread.

total.description: Unread venue messages across them all; the dot shows while above zero.

Yalla.Application.Messages.DinerUnreadTh.description: One of the guest's threads on the unread list.
